Folks,

We've been focused on voter registration all year -- it's been our number one priority, starting with reengaging lapsed voters and attracting new voters to our outreach on the ground and advertising online. Now that we've put in all that effort, our focus is starting to pivot to voter mobilization.

subject: This is what a smear campaign looks like

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

First, Rep. Rashida Tlaib was the target of a racist, Islamophobic
political cartoon in the far-right outlet, the National Review.

Next, major media outlets including CNN and the head of the
Anti-Defamation League promoted a harmful and fabricated lie about the
Congressmember, misquoting and misrepresenting her remarks about the
Michigan Attorney General issuing unjust criminal charges against student
protesters.

Then, Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel, CNN journalists Dana Bash and
Jake Tapper, and others have continued to push dangerous lies about
Rashida despite being fact-checked by the Detroit Metro Times and the
reporter of the original article they’re referring to.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jdem-20240925-rt.AShwcY&refcode=em20240925-36022&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=36022%2E1203867%2EDRfZgX ]Tweet from Steve Neavling: I’m the reporter who interviewed Rashida
Tlaib. She never said Nessel did this because she’s Jewish. Never. You’re
spreading lies.

Despite the correction, CNN reporters refuse to apologize to Rashida and
AG Nessell doubled down on her attacks despite no evidence, perpetuating
Rashida’s actual point: there is a clear anti-Palestinian attitude among
many institutions, including Congress and the media, that has become far
too normalized.

This is what a smear campaign looks like,
Peter. CNN should be ashamed for allowing its
journalists to spread blatant lies about Rashida with impunity, but
instead, it has prioritized attacking the only Palestinian American
Congresswoman over reporting the truth.

Rashida has and will always speak up for the human rights of ALL people
despite these vicious attacks against her character, and Justice Democrats

# FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
September 25, 2024
CONTACT: press@kevinfaulconer.com

**Faulconer Sets the Record Straight About Terra Lawson-Remer's Latest Attempt to Distract from Her Record of Absenteeism**
San Diego, CA – Today, Kevin Faulconer addressed Supervisor Terra Lawson-Remer’s dishonest attack on his record as Mayor, particularly her misleading claims about homelessness. Lawson-Remer, who has been absent from the job she was elected to do, continues to distort the facts while failing the people of San Diego County.
A search on google shows that Lawson-Remer is Vice Chair of San Diego County’s Regional Task Force on Homelessness Continuum of Care (CoC), yet she has not attended a single meeting. The task force, designed to promote solutions to homelessness and provide essential funding to rehouse homeless individuals, is critical to tackling the homelessness crisis. Public records show Lawson-Remer has failed to attend a single meeting since she joined the board in 2021.
---
[](https://kevinfaulconer.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c8e1915e5d9cc8e4a2f64f766&id=6a6db4a818&e=784f78234b)
| Homelessness has worsened every year since Lawson-Remer took office. In fact, the latest PIT count revealed chronic homelessness has skyrocketed every year Lawson-Remer she has been in office.)
---
| Despite holding a leadership role on the task force, Lawson-Remer has skipped a total of 199 meetings, including critical Board of Supervisors, committee, and subcommittee meetings, according to public records. Her dismal attendance record speaks volumes about her lack of commitment to addressing homelessness and many other responsibilities she has neglected.
---
| _(NBC7 shows a quote from Lawson-Remer who represents the County on the RTFH’s Continuum of Care Advisory Board as Vice Chair.)_
---
| In addition to her absences from the CoC Board, Lawson-Remer has missed 765 votes—more than all other supervisors combined—demonstrating a pattern of disregard for San Diego County's critical issues.
**Lawson-Remer’s Ongoing Pattern of Absenteeism** Her lack of commitment extends beyond the Regional Task Force on Homelessness’ CoC Advisory Board:
* SANDAG Board of Directors: [Her attendance dropped from 90% in 2021 to 50% in 2022. She missed nearly half of all votes.](https://kevinfaulconer.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c8e1915e5d9cc8e4a2f64f766&id=eefa4f068d&e=784f78234b)

* Shoreline Preservation Group: [She was the sole member assigned and attended just one meeting.](https://kevinfaulconer.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c8e1915e5d9cc8e4a2f64f766&id=b025f67e5d&e=784f78234b)

* San Diego Air Pollution Control District: [Lawson-Remer missed 60% of meetingsin 2022 and has missed every meeting in 2023 and 2024 so thusfar.](https://kevinfaulconer.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c8e1915e5d9cc8e4a2f64f766&id=4a70154c94&e=784f78234b)

* San Diego County Water Authority: [Appointed to safeguard water rates, she has neverattended a single meeting.](https://kevinfaulconer.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c8e1915e5d9cc8e4a2f64f766&id=f657db7dba&e=784f78234b)

* Mission Trails Regional Park Task Force: [Missed all but one meeting](https://kevinfaulconer.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c8e1915e5d9cc8e4a2f64f766&id=9a8d119c18&e=784f78234b).

* North San Diego County Transit Development Board: [Zero attendance](https://kevinfaulconer.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c8e1915e5d9cc8e4a2f64f766&id=65ada26078&e=784f78234b).

**Lawson-Remer’s Misleading Attacks**
Lawson-Remer has spent her time lying about Faulconer’s efforts to address homelessness, despite her own abysmal performance on the task force. She continues to show how deeply unserious she is about tackling the most pressing challenge our region faces. It’s clear she’s in above her head.
_**“Terra Lawson-Remer can’t have it both ways: you can’t say homelessness is your number one priority while attending zero meetings of County homeless task force. She has no real excuse for her terrible job performance as supervisor. She’s accepting a massive salary and benefits without doing her job,” said former mayor Kevin Faulconer, candidate for supervisor. “It’s time for her to answer for her failures, not deflect blame.”**_

# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=1969%2E135344%2Eq6foNv)

Friend --
It is almost the end of the month, and that means if you're anything like me, your inbox is filled with requests from political campaigns and organizations asking for donations.
I’d appreciate the chance to explain why a donation to my campaign for U.S. Senate is one of the most strategic contributions you can make today.
Let me start with what you probably already instinctively know: Michigan is going to be a critical state for the 2024 campaign. There is no winning the White House without Michigan. For Democrats, there is no holding the Senate without Michigan.
But you were probably already sold on the importance of Michigan. So, aside from the fact that control of the U.S. Senate is at stake (!), what about my race? Why donate to my campaign?
This is one of the rare open Senate races without an incumbent running. That means we have A LOT of introducing of me to do across the state. A recent poll showed about 50% of the state knows me, across our 11 media markets.
Reaching those folks takes resources, and that's not something I can do without you.
Add the fact that this is going to be one of the most expensive races in the country — not just with candidate spending, but outside spending too.
And I'll close with the news that in all of my elections, I have historically done better than Democrats usually do in the "redder" areas of the state. That means I am finding and pulling voters other races couldn't, and that is good for everyone up and down the ballot on Election Day.
So yes, this race is kind of a unicorn. It's a unique situation where control of the White House and Congress is on the line, most voters don't know the candidates yet, and the Democratic Senate candidate can help the top of the ticket, and not the other way around.
[**That's why I am asking for your support: Can I count on you to make a contribution to my campaign for U.S. Senate before our September FEC fundraising drive ends? I would not ask if it were not so important.**](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-sep24.1Cpmdt&refcode=em240925-4-900&t=2&akid=1969%2E135344%2Eq6foNv)

Wade, died because she couldn’t have access to this reproductive health care. It destroyed his family for decades.”' | | | | | This fall, the people get the final say on the future of abortion rights in Florida. Power-hungry Republicans like Rick Scott are TERRIFIED because they know the pro-choice turnout will be huge. | ---|---|---|--- | | | | With Scott’s approval rating tanking, a poll showing me just a point away, and this race UPGRADED to a "Toss Up," the conditions are ripe for a Democratic upset of Florida's Senate race, too. | ---|---|---|--- So i=. | | = Even with the momentum we've built together, the new awareness that will come from this article, and the data clearly showing that the tide is turning in Florida, my chances of victory ultimately come down to cold hard cash. I'm up against one of the richest senators in Washington, who spent $64 MILLION to buy this seat last time — and still only scraped by with a 10,033-vote win. And in the first half of 2024 alone, he spent over $27 million more to keep it. So with my FINAL quarterly reporting deadline of the race on Sept. 30, Scott will soon see for himself exactly how strong this movement is. That means, friend, that no matter how much positive coverage my race gets, I cannot win without the resources to fight back against Rick Scott's multimillion-dollar ad spending. And since I don't have a nine-figure fortune, my success is riding on grassroots supporters like you.= Please use the links in this email to start a weekly donation through ActBlue. | | | = | | = | | = | | = I couldn't have come this far without you — thank you, Debbie | * | | | = Debbie Mucarsel-Powell is a Floridian, South American immigrant, mother, and former Congresswoman. She’s dedicated her life to uplifting working families, ending gun violence, and fighting for her community. Now, she’s running to defeat Republican Senator Rick Scott and win a better, brighter future for Florida.

name: Clint St. Mosley for Congress
subject: Clint St. Mosley: Update from Michigan's 9th Congressional District
body:
Clint St. Mosley Campaign Update from Michigan's 9th Congressional District | | | | |
---
|
# Greetings from the Campaign Trail!
---
| | | | | Hello everyone and thank you for supporting our campaign!
With just 41 days to go, this is likely to be the one of most consequential weeks of our campaign as more than 115,000 absentee ballots will be mailed out to voters across the 9th Congressional District in the coming days.
Because of the importance of reaching them, we’ve launched an all-out blitz that includes digital and social media ads targeted to likely AV voters and amped-up canvassing that starts this Saturday across the district.
And our order of 1,000 more signs has arrived!
We also hired a field operations director, Tom Cruz, who is helping us organize canvassing, phone/text banking and precinct delegate volunteers. (And may be repelling from a helicopter along the way!)
So if you’d like to volunteer to help put end to Lisa McClains’ MAGA Madness and restore civility in Washington, sign up [**HERE**](https://clint4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e73040a2243d332c2516e1117&id=0cf78559fa&e=21c900a6be)! We’ll connect you with Tom to help get you going a.s.a.p.
While we’re feeling good on these fronts, we’re still behind our targets to get campaign lit mailed to these voters. At nearly $1 each across 85,000 AV addresses, this is one of our largest expenses of the campaign and remains an uphill battle.
[**CLICK HERE**](https://clint4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e73040a2243d332c2516e1117&id=7ac76b2b6a&e=21c900a6be) if this is something you can help us cover.
**Student Absentee Voters** On the topic of AV/mail-in voters, one group vital to Democrats are young voters and college students. The good news is, Michigan has among the highest percentage of registered voters ages 18-25 in the U.S.
The bad news: this group tends to have the lowest voter turnout of any age group.
Parents, please make a plan to get your kids a mail-in ballot and get it to them. Remind them to vote _and_ fill out the ballot on both sides. Reach out to your local Dem club for slate cards if you need them.
**Trickle-Down Economics is DOA** When out canvassing, let’s remember that Democrats have a strong economic story to tell undecided voters. Without getting into the weeds here’s where we win:
First, Trickle-Down Economics has been a complete disaster for working class families since Reagan rolled it out over 40 years ago. All it did was turn millionaires into billionaires, and destroyed the middle class while helping put our country in massive debt.
Democrats are focusing on the Opportunity Economy that prioritizes working families first by growing our economy from the bottom up, and middle out. That’s what the Biden/Harris administration has done with investments in infrastructure, the CHIPs and Science Act and the Inflation Reduction Act.
All of these programs are why manufacturing jobs in Michigan are at record highs and wages are up while unemployment remains historically low.
I also often hear from voters that Joe Biden caused inflation. That again, is not true. Inflation began during Covid due to supply chain interruptions and labor shortages. However, under Biden and Harris, America tamped-down inflation FASTER than any other country.
And once again, America is the LARGEST economy in the world! Plus the stock market is up, growth is strong and we avoided the recession that many predicted.
Now that inflation is in-check, interest rates are coming down, and so too are the costs of goods and housing. Yes, we’ve got a lot more to do, but let’s stand strong on the economic gains Democrats have delivered to working families.
**On the Campaign Trail** I had an awesome time at the St. Clair County Democratic Party Fall Solidarity Brunch at the St. Clair Inn. It was an amazing event with guest speakers Rep. David Bonior (ret.) and Kyra Harris Bolden, who is running for the Michigan Supreme Court.
My thanks to SCCDP chair Jim Frank and the event committee for allowing me to speak and for organizing one of the best group of Democrats I’ve seen in a long time!
**Upcoming Events****9/30 Caseville** : Thumb Brewery Meet & Greet on Monday, Sept. 30 from 5-7 p.m., at 6758 Pine St, Caseville, MI, United States, Michigan[ _**EVENT LINK**_](https://clint4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e73040a2243d332c2516e1117&id=c58c4244c7&e=21c900a6be)
**10/4 Holly** : Holly Fundraiser for Clint St. Mosley 4Congress, Friday, Oct. 4 from 5:30-7 p.m. at Funky Fungi’s Tea House, 113 Battle Aly, Holly, MI. [_**EVENT LINK**_](https://clint4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e73040a2243d332c2516e1117&id=745f156583&e=21c900a6be)
_If you’d like to host or organize an event in your area, please reach out Sara DiGiglio at_[ _sara@clint4congress.com_](mailto:sara@clint4congress.com) _and she’ll help get you get things going._
If you have questions or would like to discuss issues important to you, contact me at [hello@clint4congress.com](mailto:hello@clint4congress.com) and we’ll connect.
Again, as always, I am eternally grateful for all the help and support you’ve given our campaign. As every day passes, we meet more enthusiastic supporters who are energized by the Harris/Walz ticket and are motivated to bring the positive change we need for our district in November!
Sincerely,
Clint St. MosleyDemocratic CandidateMichigan’s 9th Congressional District

**We got a wake-up call in 2012, Peter:** The GOP used map manipulation to choose their voters. Democrats in the U.S. House earned 1.4 million _more_ votes than their Republican opponents — but ended up with 33 _fewer_ seats.
Republicans used this electoral advantage to obstruct President Obama's agenda. Across the country, gerrymandered maps allowed radical lawmakers to restrict access to abortion, block common-sense gun safety measures, and make it harder for people to vote.
So the NDRC got to work, too:
* We rallied fair maps supporters around the country.
* We helped elect candidates who could ensure fair redistricting processes.
* We helped states enact reforms.

And our work... well... _worked_. _The New York Times_ called the 2022 congressional maps the fairest in 50 years.

* **TOP NEWS**

**" Texas' growth at risk due to water shortages, urgent action needed,"** KXAN's**Ryan Chandler** -- "In Wimberley, boulders and deer bones bake in the heat where there was once a thriving creek. The lakes and rivers that once attracted Texans and enabled them to grow communities there are drying up, posing an active but underappreciated emergency that sets a limit on the "Texas Miracle," state leaders say.

"Texas is out of water," Texas Agriculture Commissioner **Sid Miller** told Nexstar on Tuesday. "We can't grow, we can't expand, we can't have economic opportunity and jobs without water. We've reached our limit, there is no more. We've got to do some things different."

Wimberley and much of Central Texas has been in a drought for most of the last two years. It has led some local officials to implement Stage 4 water restrictions, where residents are penalized for automatic water sprinklers and watering is confined to certain times. But out in West Texas, conditions are far worse.

Miller said Texas loses about one farm every week, but it's not for lack of land. Farmers don't have enough water to keep their crops alive.

Texas's population is expected to gain over 22 million people by 2070, according to the 2022 [Texas State Water Plan](https://substack.com/redirect/1a8f6317-fa9d-4e3f-a31d-078e35f42ac0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Over the same period, the water supply is projected to decrease by 18%.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/2cc0ec96-3363-48e3-9291-29e0b34f381b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[The National Wildlife Federation](https://substack.com/redirect/1dc31904-7a8d-4ec9-b7db-0c633a8b2bb4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found Texas loses 572,000 acre-feet of water per year -- enough to fill almost 240 AT&T Stadiums and supply Austin, Fort Worth, El Paso, Laredo, and Lubbock combined for an entire year. As Texas regularly faces drought periods, some lawmakers are urging the state to proactively protect the most valuable resource.

"It's the silent issue, with the least urgency, with the biggest impact," State Sen. **Charles Perry** , R-Lubbock, previously told Nexstar. "We've been, for far too long, treating water like a commodity that has no meaning. And it's truly not. It's not a commodity. It's a necessity."

On Tuesday, state lawmakers tasked with shepherding natural resources reviewed the implementation of the Texas Water Fund, which dedicated a billion dollars to water conservation projects across the state. But that sum is, for lack of a better term, a drop in the bucket.

Perry, one of the legislature's longtime champions of water conservation, expects it will take billions more.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/2cc0ec96-3363-48e3-9291-29e0b34f381b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
"Water is the only problem that we face as a state that can literally be fixed with more money," Sen. Perry said. "It's just a commitment to a vision to provide water and a commitment of resources to get there. So that's been my frustration -- it's not one of those problems that we can't solve. The lack of urgency to deal with it is frustrating."

On Tuesday, Commissioner Miller pointed to multiple tangible ways to save water -- the first is hard infrastructure upgrades. Leaky pipes alone waste more than 130 billion gallons of water every year, the Texas Water Development Board found.

Fracking is also a focus -- using clean water to frack wastes and pollutes, and Miller said more companies are transitioning to brackish water.

"We've got a lot to do," he said. "We've just got to get busy and help ourselves."" [KXAN](https://substack.com/redirect/c7682158-98f7-4f18-9ecf-4277c63726fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* **BUSINESS NEWS**

**" San Antonio's USAA is laying off more employees,"** San Antonio Express-News'**Madison Iszler** -- "USAA -- one of San Antonio's largest employers -- has issued another round of pink slips.

The [insurance and financial services company](https://substack.com/redirect/89bf6e60-87eb-4223-ab71-dd1af3532c83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) confirmed Tuesday it had laid off more employees but did not disclose how many or which departments were affected. Online chatter suggested workers at [USAA Federal Savings Bank](https://substack.com/redirect/fb9712c9-14f5-4db2-9718-9f28c737c682?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and in compliance and consumer lending were among those laid off.

"We regularly evaluate our operations and adjust to serve our members more efficiently," said spokesperson **Roger Wildermuth**. "USAA continues to hire across the company in line with changing business needs, including more than 8,300 jobs filled so far this year, and remains focused on providing our members with exceptional products and service."

The cuts mark the company's second round of layoffs this year after it [cut 220 employees in April](https://substack.com/redirect/b553f997-1c10-4dca-a9be-724711e5ab4c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). It's at least the seventh round since March 2022, decisions USAA has attributed to "changing business needs," a tepid national housing market and slowing global economy.

USAA has more than 37,000 employees nationwide, including about 19,000 in the San Antonio area.

The cuts come on the heels of President and CEO **Wayne Peacock 's** [recent announcement](https://substack.com/redirect/d271bbbc-fc0b-43d7-b980-58ed238eb1ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that he plans to retire in the first half of 2025 after 36 years at the company. USAA has said it is vetting internal and external candidates to replace Peacock, who's been CEO since 2020.

USAA [reported a profit](https://substack.com/redirect/f666c6a5-759c-4c6e-83a5-5b61929536f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of $1.2 billion in 2023, up from a loss of $1.3 billion in 2022 but down from a profit of $3.3 billion in 2021, according to the company's most recent annual financial report. Revenue reached a record $42.5 billion.

The company provides insurance, banking and retirement solutions to more than 13 million members of the military, veterans and their families." [SAEN](https://substack.com/redirect/c708b999-8d35-4da1-971e-06d77503f867?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)
* * *
* **STATE GOVERNMENT**

**" Appeals court says Texas State Fair can ban guns,"** Texas Tribune's **Juan Salinas II** -- "A newly created state appeals court denied Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** request to temporarily block the State Fair of Texas' policy banning all firearms from its fairgrounds as the event is set to start Friday.

The ruling comes after a Dallas County District Court struck down a similar request from Paxton on the new policy. The District Court Judge agreed with State Fair officials that they could enforce a gun ban as a private nonprofit.

Paxton says the fair's gun ban violates state law, which bars most government bodies from prohibiting weapons. State Fair officials say it has the right as a private nonprofit, and the city of Dallas says it has no role in the fair's gun policy.

Paxton said on social media Tuesday evening that he will next ask the Texas Supreme Court to overturn the ban.

The State Fair begins Friday." [Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/fc70b618-07ca-4f66-bf3b-e6d46b9fa2c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* **LOCAL GOVERNMENT**

**" Dallas council members request an audit of failed lead abatement program,"** Dallas Morning News' **Maria Ramos Pacheco** -- "Two Dallas council members requested an audit into the $2.3 million failed city's lead removal program after The Dallas Morning News [investigated](https://substack.com/redirect/85f162c1-d6cd-4619-9621-30d578af784f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its outcome, which left multiple residents exposed to lead.

District 13 Councilmember **Gay Donnell Willis** and District 1 Councilmember **Chad West** sent a memorandum on Sept. 16 to City Auditor **Mark Swann** asking him to add the program to his work plan and examine it more closely.

"The audit should focus on [identifying the causes of program delays,](https://substack.com/redirect/ae76422f-1fa7-4177-92f9-4881374769c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) inefficiencies in executing lead removal, and the lack of contractor availability in Dallas versus other cities where the program has been successful. It should also assess communication with residents and other stakeholders throughout the process," read the memo.

Willis and West did not respond to a request for comment.

_The News_ reached out to **Cynthia Rogers-Ellickson** , interim director of the housing and neighborhood revitalization department, and **Thor Erickson** , the department's assistant director, via email but did not respond to a request for comment.

The city's communication department said via email the managers in the housing department were aware of the audit and would assist the auditor in his review and provide any information requested.

The Office of the City Auditor's Recommended Fiscal Year 2025 Audit Work Plan includes an audit of the lead abatement program. The work plan will be subject to final approval by the full City Council on Oct. 23. After the Work Plan is approved, the audit will be scheduled to start when audit resources are available, said Swann via email." [DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/cb19c870-5ce4-42f9-b745-8528938e3ce3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)

**" While Bexar County barrels toward fiscal 'cliff,' San Antonio sees smoother landing,"** San Antonio Report's **Iris Dimmick** -- "The City of San Antonio put the finishing touches on its [nearly $4 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/12f62e53-c223-40a9-8d54-b5fed26af409?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) fiscal year 2025 budget on Thursday -- and with that, pledged the last scraps of its federal coronavirus pandemic recovery fund.

The city allocated its remaining $5.8 million in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding on one-time expenses, including expanding senior center hours, [relocation assistance](https://substack.com/redirect/29d49ac2-4dfa-4549-b44b-f77063b3df31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for downtown residents and seed funding for a [South Side health equity initiative](https://substack.com/redirect/68975dd6-710a-42c5-8dfb-ed16e4dc4c52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

Meanwhile, Bexar County adopted a $2.8 billion budget [one week earlier](https://substack.com/redirect/fc5b0c4b-0f82-4974-8dbd-acd22191b337?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that sets the county on course toward a so-called "[ARPA cliff](https://substack.com/redirect/ef6ad2aa-824f-45b9-a5c5-a4a387cd4e03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" unless serious cuts are made or revenue is generated. The county used its last remaining ARPA funds to plug an $18.8 million hole in its general fund budget -- rather than using it for new one-time expenses, as commissioners had previously discussed.

Between the newly established [public health department](https://substack.com/redirect/1cff2e81-9ce8-4ec5-b6a5-47a541473146?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [expanded mental health law enforcement](https://substack.com/redirect/3fa50312-57da-4c6f-bf4f-a058375027b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) program and other initiatives that require reoccurring expenses, the county has bitten off more than its budget can afford in future years without ARPA support.

"How many of those ARPA-funded programs continue in the future" will come down to policy decisions made by the Bexar County Commissioners Court, County Manager **David Smith** said. "As soon as next budget, we're going to have to start examining some of those potential impacts."

The city was careful not to over-extend itself, City Manager **Erik Walsh** said. It ramped up existing programs that it could wind down once funding ran out. The budget deficit that the city had to deal with this year, for the first time since 2010, was due to [slowing revenue growth](https://substack.com/redirect/18d61708-aa6c-4fb0-8e12-4291c8e39bd6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from both property and sales taxes -- not as a result of its dwindling ARPA funds.

"We've planned appropriately for ARPA over the last couple of years and we'll continue to plan for the next year and a half," Walsh said.

"Some cities added firefighters or police officers," he added. "I don't know what the heck they're going to do when that money dries out."" [SA Report](https://substack.com/redirect/68a37d05-e9da-41fd-8bd9-82554d8dca80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

**" Fort Worth ISD school board accepts voluntary resignation of Superintendent Angelica Ramsey,"** Fort Worth Report's **Jacob Sanchez** and **Matthew Sgroi** -- "The Angelica Ramsey-led era of Fort Worth ISD is over after the school board accepted her voluntary resignation.

Trustees' 8-1 vote on Sept. 24 came almost to the day two years ago that trustees formally hired Ramsey, who [entered the superintendency with high hopes](https://substack.com/redirect/2374c80a-2ebd-48a9-8b8b-5df87b4c86e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of improving academic achievement and the district's financial standing. She now leaves the district amid criticism of unchanged student outcomes, a $17.7 million deficit budget and [teachers who say they feel overburdened](https://substack.com/redirect/338a0deb-21c2-495a-b848-1af3e8d70aba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by district mandates.

The sole dissenting vote was trustee **Camille Rodriguez**. The board members came out of a more than three-hour executive session and announced the resignation without comment.

Ramsey's resignation as superintendent is effective Oct. 1, according to a joint statement from the school board and the departing leader. However, she will remain a Fort Worth ISD employee until Aug. 30, 2025.

The school board plans to appoint an interim superintendent. The interim leader will remain in the position as trustees search for a new superintendent.

During a news conference, school board President **Roxanne Martinez** thanked Ramsey for her service and said trustees will move forward with a focus on improving student achievement.

Martinez explained her vote to accept Ramsey's resignation.

"Hearing the community's concerns was a large part of why I supported the decision. I also think we mutually made a decision to move on in the best interest of children," Martinez said. "That's what my focus is going to be as president -- moving forward and improving student achievement just like our community and our parents wish to see."

In a [four-page statement](https://substack.com/redirect/d9589531-4054-4635-af9e-53ea0bf383c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Ramsey listed what she saw as her achievements as Fort Worth ISD's superintendent for the past two years, such as improvements seen in the [district's self-assigned A-F ratings](https://substack.com/redirect/1f2e5404-f4e6-4ec0-a05a-cadc63206923?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

"I would like to extend my deepest gratitude to the Fort Worth ISD board for allowing me the honor of serving this district over the past two years. It has been a privilege, and I have approached this responsibility with the utmost seriousness and dedication," Ramsey said."

The pressure put on Ramsey and her leadership had intensified in recent weeks after more than 40 community leaders called for a district turnaround plan. On Aug. 27, in a letter and a [speech to the school board](https://substack.com/redirect/7c1b7087-393c-464a-b790-b636172b0748?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Mayor **Mattie Parker** voiced dissatisfaction with the lackluster and stagnant state of the district.

Those critical of Ramsey's tenure also noted empty promises when it came to improving [literacy rates for Black](https://substack.com/redirect/aea6ba40-d661-49db-a8d3-afe0f36f97a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and Hispanic students. Trustee **Wallace Bridges** voiced his concerns over the district's lack of progress in improving reading rates for Black students during school board meetings. For two years, the district has not had a plan for these students, he said." [FW Report](https://substack.com/redirect/a0e35b64-3a1f-4560-99ac-c03452035cf1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* **2024**

**" Ted Cruz is again fighting for political survival in Texas,"** New York Times'**J. David Goodman** -- "On a late summer afternoon, **Colin Allred** , the Democratic challenger to U.S. Senator **Ted Cruz** of Texas, mingled his way through a barbershop in a historically Black neighborhood of Houston.

As he did so, a barber confessed that he had never heard of Mr. Allred, a Dallas congressman and former N.F.L. linebacker, until he was told the candidate would be coming by the shop. Neither had his client.

"Everybody knows Ted," said the barber, **Christopher Williams**. "He's not giving nothing up. It's going to be a fight, and I love a good fight."

In recent weeks, the race for U.S. Senate in Texas has grown increasingly competitive, with negative ads appearing with every channel flip and public polls showing a contest within single digits. Mr. Cruz, who is running for a third term, has been leading, but he attracts less support than former President **Donald J. Trump** does.

So what may have seemed like a sure thing for Republicans in the Republican-dominated state has some party officials in Texas concerned.

"The current reality is that Texas is too close for comfort," **Matt Mackowiak** , head of the Travis County Republican Party, said in [a letter to state party leaders](https://substack.com/redirect/b741f97f-9891-4600-832c-8cd3bbea542c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

The race is on track to be one of the most expensive in state history. But among Democrats, it has still not generated anything like the fervor or attention of 2018, when another little-known congressman, **Beto O 'Rourke**, barnstormed his way to nearly defeating Mr. Cruz.

Mr. O'Rourke's near victory is still frequently mentioned by Texas Democrats, the what-could-have-been moment that, in other elections since, they have been chasing and failing to replicate. A Democrat has not won statewide in Texas in 30 years.

But the near defeat has fueled Mr. Cruz's determination not to let Republicans get overconfident this time. He has been trying to pull off a difficult political trick for a politician whose name ID is nearly universal: to remake his firebrand persona into something more approachable.

"They're going to tell you I am a horrible creature who devours kittens at sunrise, which is ridiculous," Mr. Cruz told campaign volunteers earlier this year, joking about his image in the media months before Republicans began accusing migrants in Ohio of eating pets. "Everyone knows you eat kittens at _night_."

The senator's campaign has worried that a close race down the stretch could invite new rounds of investment from Democrats, and that some middle-of-the-road Texas voters, unsatisfied with either Mr. Trump or his Democratic rival, Vice President **Kamala Harris** , may nevertheless vote in the Senate race.

That has led to a big fight over voters in the middle. Both candidates have tried to claim the mantle of bipartisanship. Both have rolled out endorsements by members of the opposite party.

**Liz Cheney** , the former Republican representative from Wyoming, is backing Mr. Allred.**Kim Ogg** , the Democratic district attorney for Harris County, which includes Houston, has been [vocal in her support for Mr. Cruz](https://substack.com/redirect/0ca0ff6b-ab12-4780-8197-5f70f7ba54ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

Mr. Allred has demonstrated an ability to raise money to bombard the airwaves with ads and a willingness to go on the attack against Mr. Cruz.

Perhaps never has a race for Senate included so many mentions of Cancun, Mexico, where Mr. Cruz went vacationing during a 2021 winter storm in Texas that left more than 200 people dead. Mr. Allred finds ways to bring it up whenever possible, [including in an ad about Social Security and Medicare](https://substack.com/redirect/cf64b9cd-ec30-460e-9006-b15de4744b47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Mr. Allred, 41, played linebacker for the Tennessee Titans before becoming a lawyer. In 2018, he [defeated a Republican incumbent in a close race](https://substack.com/redirect/1624bb47-284f-427b-9300-8ab83c34ffb9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to win his congressional seat in Dallas.

"Change can happen quickly in Texas," Mr. Allred, who is Black, said in an interview in which he talked about the diversity of the state. "What we have to do in Texas is embrace who we actually are, which is that diversity and that complexity that comes with it. Instead of being afraid of it."

A first debate in the race is scheduled for Oct. 15." " [NYT](https://substack.com/redirect/d70f3cfa-cec9-4dae-b7b9-ef897c61da20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

**" Colin Allred, Ted Cruz spar over credit for microchip bill,"** Dallas Morning News'**Joseph Morton** -- "U.S. Sen. **Ted Cruz** , R-Texas, and his Democratic challenger, U.S. Rep. **Colin Allred** of Dallas, agree that Texas can expect new jobs and economic development from a bill easing permitting requirements on new [semiconductor manufacturing facilities](https://substack.com/redirect/f1c87a78-8d0d-46ef-8e49-eb12a3c065b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

The two sparred sharply this week, however, over which of them deserves credit for getting the legislation to President **Joe Biden 's** desk.

Allred's camp noted that he [co-sponsored the original House bill](https://substack.com/redirect/974c1036-ac96-4063-abf7-099542520d6f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Cruz said he rewrote it in the Senate and convinced House GOP leaders to push his version over the finish line.

The dispute comes as the two candidates are locked in a competitive race, with each pitching himself as the best option to deliver on job creation.

"A win for Texas! The House passed our bill, the Building Chips in America Act, to streamline permitting and advance CHIPS Act projects," [Allred said on X](https://substack.com/redirect/29b0b040-f532-42df-8f9b-3d0742129e34?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). "Thanks to a team from both sides of the aisle, we got this done."

Repeating his criticism that Cruz is more interested in self-promotion than finding solutions, Allred added: "Ted Cruz is trying to claim credit. Classic Ted acting like a 'me guy.' "

A prime example, Allred says, was Cruz's vote against the[ 2022 CHIPS and Science Act](https://substack.com/redirect/bc27587d-d119-4166-8374-7674ecc2ffa0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that was intended to boost [domestic production of microchips](https://substack.com/redirect/993d6b25-482a-46de-abc7-fe991e91a938?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and is helping bring billions of dollars to new Texas facilities.

Cruz says he enthusiastically supported the 2022 bill's tax and regulatory incentives for new manufacturing facilities but strongly objected to its direct corporate subsidies.

"I am not a fan of giving taxpayer money directly to private corporations, and I think history has shown that it can lead to bad results," Cruz said. "Once the bill passed, I have actively urged as many of those dollars as possible to go to Texas."

Cruz said he was particularly interested in speeding those new manufacturing facilities through a federal environmental review process that can delay projects for years.

He recounted seeing an Allred news release announcing the original proposal to ease those requirements.

Cruz said some of the original language would have disadvantaged Texas, so he blocked it and asked his staff to write new language.

He worked with U.S. Sen. **Mark Kelly** , D-Ariz., to get that version unanimously approved by the Senate.

The reworked bill encountered resistance in the House from some Democrats concerned about undermining environmental regulations and from some Republicans who wanted a more comprehensive overhaul of environmental rules.

The House voted 257-125 Monday to approve the Cruz-Kelly version.

In an interview, Cruz talked in great detail about the various legislative twists and turns the permitting bill went through on the way to final passage as he lobbied for support in the House and urged House Speaker **Mike Johnson** , R-La., to bring the bill to the floor.

It is "utterly bizarre" that Allred would claim the legislation as his own, he said.

"The fact that Colin Allred is trying to claim credit for legislation that I drafted and that I have been fighting a year to pass is emblematic of his campaign," Cruz said.

He said Allred is trying to pitch himself as a bipartisan-minded moderate despite voting consistently with his party for years, particularly in opposition to Republican proposals to secure the border and stem illegal immigration." ($5/mo or $50/yr or $199 lifetime) TOP NEWS " Texas' growth at risk due to water shortages, urgent action needed," KXAN'sRyan Chandler -- "In Wimberley, boulders and deer bones bake in the heat where there was once a thriving creek. The lakes and rivers that once attracted Texans and enabled them to grow communities there are drying up, posing an active but underappreciated emergency that sets a limit on the "Texas Miracle," state leaders say. "Texas is out of water," Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller told Nexstar on Tuesday. "We can't grow, we can't expand, we can't have economic opportunity and jobs without water. We've reached our limit, there is no more. We've got to do some things different." Wimberley and much of Central Texas has been in a drought for most of the last two years. It has led some local officials to implement Stage 4 water restrictions, where residents are penalized for automatic water sprinklers and watering is confined to certain times. But out in West Texas, conditions are far worse. Miller said Texas loses about one farm every week, but it's not for lack of land. Farmers don't have enough water to keep their crops alive. Texas's population is expected to gain over 22 million people by 2070, according to the 2022 . Over the same period, the water supply is projected to decrease by 18%. found Texas loses 572,000 acre-feet of water per year -- enough to fill almost 240 AT&T Stadiums and supply Austin, Fort Worth, El Paso, Laredo, and Lubbock combined for an entire year. As Texas regularly faces drought periods, some lawmakers are urging the state to proactively protect the most valuable resource. "It's the silent issue, with the least urgency, with the biggest impact," State Sen. Charles Perry , R-Lubbock, previously told Nexstar. "We've been, for far too long, treating water like a commodity that has no meaning. And it's truly not. It's not a commodity. It's a necessity." On Tuesday, state lawmakers tasked with shepherding natural resources reviewed the implementation of the Texas Water Fund, which dedicated a billion dollars to water conservation projects across the state. But that sum is, for lack of a better term, a drop in the bucket. Perry, one of the legislature's longtime champions of water conservation, expects it will take billions more. "Water is the only problem that we face as a state that can literally be fixed with more money," Sen. Perry said. "It's just a commitment to a vision to provide water and a commitment of resources to get there. So that's been my frustration -- it's not one of those problems that we can't solve. The lack of urgency to deal with it is frustrating." On Tuesday, Commissioner Miller pointed to multiple tangible ways to save water -- the first is hard infrastructure upgrades. Leaky pipes alone waste more than 130 billion gallons of water every year, the Texas Water Development Board found. Fracking is also a focus -- using clean water to frack wastes and pollutes, and Miller said more companies are transitioning to brackish water. "We've got a lot to do," he said. "We've just got to get busy and help ourselves."" BUSINESS NEWS " San Antonio's USAA is laying off more employees," San Antonio Express-News'Madison Iszler -- "USAA -- one of San Antonio's largest employers -- has issued another round of pink slips. The confirmed Tuesday it had laid off more employees but did not disclose how many or which departments were affected. Online chatter suggested workers at and in compliance and consumer lending were among those laid off. "We regularly evaluate our operations and adjust to serve our members more efficiently," said spokesperson Roger Wildermuth. "USAA continues to hire across the company in line with changing business needs, including more than 8,300 jobs filled so far this year, and remains focused on providing our members with exceptional products and service." The cuts mark the company's second round of layoffs this year after it . It's at least the seventh round since March 2022, decisions USAA has attributed to "changing business needs," a tepid national housing market and slowing global economy. USAA has more than 37,000 employees nationwide, including about 19,000 in the San Antonio area. The cuts come on the heels of President and CEO Wayne Peacock 's that he plans to retire in the first half of 2025 after 36 years at the company. USAA has said it is vetting internal and external candidates to replace Peacock, who's been CEO since 2020. USAA of $1.2 billion in 2023, up from a loss of $1.3 billion in 2022 but down from a profit of $3.3 billion in 2021, according to the company's most recent annual financial report. Revenue reached a record $42.5 billion. The company provides insurance, banking and retirement solutions to more than 13 million members of the military, veterans and their families." ($) STATE GOVERNMENT " Appeals court says Texas State Fair can ban guns," Texas Tribune's Juan Salinas II -- "A newly created state appeals court denied Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton request to temporarily block the State Fair of Texas' policy banning all firearms from its fairgrounds as the event is set to start Friday. The ruling comes after a Dallas County District Court struck down a similar request from Paxton on the new policy. The District Court Judge agreed with State Fair officials that they could enforce a gun ban as a private nonprofit. Paxton says the fair's gun ban violates state law, which bars most government bodies from prohibiting weapons. State Fair officials say it has the right as a private nonprofit, and the city of Dallas says it has no role in the fair's gun policy. Paxton said on social media Tuesday evening that he will next ask the Texas Supreme Court to overturn the ban. The State Fair begins Friday." LOCAL GOVERNMENT " Dallas council members request an audit of failed lead abatement program," Dallas Morning News' Maria Ramos Pacheco -- "Two Dallas council members requested an audit into the $2.3 million failed city's lead removal program after The Dallas Morning News its outcome, which left multiple residents exposed to lead. District 13 Councilmember Gay Donnell Willis and District 1 Councilmember Chad West sent a memorandum on Sept. 16 to City Auditor Mark Swann asking him to add the program to his work plan and examine it more closely. "The audit should focus on inefficiencies in executing lead removal, and the lack of contractor availability in Dallas versus other cities where the program has been successful. It should also assess communication with residents and other stakeholders throughout the process," read the memo. Willis and West did not respond to a request for comment. The News reached out to Cynthia Rogers-Ellickson , interim director of the housing and neighborhood revitalization department, and Thor Erickson , the department's assistant director, via email but did not respond to a request for comment. The city's communication department said via email the managers in the housing department were aware of the audit and would assist the auditor in his review and provide any information requested. The Office of the City Auditor's Recommended Fiscal Year 2025 Audit Work Plan includes an audit of the lead abatement program. The work plan will be subject to final approval by the full City Council on Oct. 23. After the Work Plan is approved, the audit will be scheduled to start when audit resources are available, said Swann via email." ($) " While Bexar County barrels toward fiscal 'cliff,' San Antonio sees smoother landing," San Antonio Report's Iris Dimmick -- "The City of San Antonio put the finishing touches on its fiscal year 2025 budget on Thursday -- and with that, pledged the last scraps of its federal coronavirus pandemic recovery fund. The city allocated its remaining $5.8 million in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding on one-time expenses, including expanding senior center hours, for downtown residents and seed funding for a . Meanwhile, Bexar County adopted a $2.8 billion budget that sets the county on course toward a so-called "" unless serious cuts are made or revenue is generated. The county used its last remaining ARPA funds to plug an $18.8 million hole in its general fund budget -- rather than using it for new one-time expenses, as commissioners had previously discussed. Between the newly established , program and other initiatives that require reoccurring expenses, the county has bitten off more than its budget can afford in future years without ARPA support. "How many of those ARPA-funded programs continue in the future" will come down to policy decisions made by the Bexar County Commissioners Court, County Manager David Smith said. "As soon as next budget, we're going to have to start examining some of those potential impacts." The city was careful not to over-extend itself, City Manager Erik Walsh said. It ramped up existing programs that it could wind down once funding ran out. The budget deficit that the city had to deal with this year, for the first time since 2010, was due to from both property and sales taxes -- not as a result of its dwindling ARPA funds. "We've planned appropriately for ARPA over the last couple of years and we'll continue to plan for the next year and a half," Walsh said. "Some cities added firefighters or police officers," he added. "I don't know what the heck they're going to do when that money dries out."" " Fort Worth ISD school board accepts voluntary resignation of Superintendent Angelica Ramsey," Fort Worth Report's Jacob Sanchez and Matthew Sgroi -- "The Angelica Ramsey-led era of Fort Worth ISD is over after the school board accepted her voluntary resignation. Trustees' 8-1 vote on Sept. 24 came almost to the day two years ago that trustees formally hired Ramsey, who of improving academic achievement and the district's financial standing. She now leaves the district amid criticism of unchanged student outcomes, a $17.7 million deficit budget and by district mandates. The sole dissenting vote was trustee Camille Rodriguez. The board members came out of a more than three-hour executive session and announced the resignation without comment. Ramsey's resignation as superintendent is effective Oct. 1, according to a joint statement from the school board and the departing leader. However, she will remain a Fort Worth ISD employee until Aug. 30, 2025. The school board plans to appoint an interim superintendent. The interim leader will remain in the position as trustees search for a new superintendent. During a news conference, school board President Roxanne Martinez thanked Ramsey for her service and said trustees will move forward with a focus on improving student achievement. Martinez explained her vote to accept Ramsey's resignation. "Hearing the community's concerns was a large part of why I supported the decision. I also think we mutually made a decision to move on in the best interest of children," Martinez said. "That's what my focus is going to be as president -- moving forward and improving student achievement just like our community and our parents wish to see." In a , Ramsey listed what she saw as her achievements as Fort Worth ISD's superintendent for the past two years, such as improvements seen in the . "I would like to extend my deepest gratitude to the Fort Worth ISD board for allowing me the honor of serving this district over the past two years. It has been a privilege, and I have approached this responsibility with the utmost seriousness and dedication," Ramsey said." The pressure put on Ramsey and her leadership had intensified in recent weeks after more than 40 community leaders called for a district turnaround plan. On Aug. 27, in a letter and a , Mayor Mattie Parker voiced dissatisfaction with the lackluster and stagnant state of the district. Those critical of Ramsey's tenure also noted empty promises when it came to improving and Hispanic students. Trustee Wallace Bridges voiced his concerns over the district's lack of progress in improving reading rates for Black students during school board meetings. For two years, the district has not had a plan for these students, he said." 2024 " Ted Cruz is again fighting for political survival in Texas," New York Times'J. David Goodman -- "On a late summer afternoon, Colin Allred , the Democratic challenger to U.S. Senator Ted Cruz of Texas, mingled his way through a barbershop in a historically Black neighborhood of Houston. As he did so, a barber confessed that he had never heard of Mr. Allred, a Dallas congressman and former N.F.L. linebacker, until he was told the candidate would be coming by the shop. Neither had his client. "Everybody knows Ted," said the barber, Christopher Williams. "He's not giving nothing up. It's going to be a fight, and I love a good fight." In recent weeks, the race for U.S. Senate in Texas has grown increasingly competitive, with negative ads appearing with every channel flip and public polls showing a contest within single digits. Mr. Cruz, who is running for a third term, has been leading, but he attracts less support than former President Donald J. Trump does. So what may have seemed like a sure thing for Republicans in the Republican-dominated state has some party officials in Texas concerned. "The current reality is that Texas is too close for comfort," Matt Mackowiak , head of the Travis County Republican Party, said in . The race is on track to be one of the most expensive in state history. But among Democrats, it has still not generated anything like the fervor or attention of 2018, when another little-known congressman, Beto O 'Rourke, barnstormed his way to nearly defeating Mr. Cruz. Mr. O'Rourke's near victory is still frequently mentioned by Texas Democrats, the what-could-have-been moment that, in other elections since, they have been chasing and failing to replicate. A Democrat has not won statewide in Texas in 30 years. But the near defeat has fueled Mr. Cruz's determination not to let Republicans get overconfident this time. He has been trying to pull off a difficult political trick for a politician whose name ID is nearly universal: to remake his firebrand persona into something more approachable. "They're going to tell you I am a horrible creature who devours kittens at sunrise, which is ridiculous," Mr. Cruz told campaign volunteers earlier this year, joking about his image in the media months before Republicans began accusing migrants in Ohio of eating pets. "Everyone knows you eat kittens at night." The senator's campaign has worried that a close race down the stretch could invite new rounds of investment from Democrats, and that some middle-of-the-road Texas voters, unsatisfied with either Mr. Trump or his Democratic rival, Vice President Kamala Harris , may nevertheless vote in the Senate race. That has led to a big fight over voters in the middle. Both candidates have tried to claim the mantle of bipartisanship. Both have rolled out endorsements by members of the opposite party. Liz Cheney , the former Republican representative from Wyoming, is backing Mr. Allred.Kim Ogg , the Democratic district attorney for Harris County, which includes Houston, has been . Mr. Allred has demonstrated an ability to raise money to bombard the airwaves with ads and a willingness to go on the attack against Mr. Cruz. Perhaps never has a race for Senate included so many mentions of Cancun, Mexico, where Mr. Cruz went vacationing during a 2021 winter storm in Texas that left more than 200 people dead. Mr. Allred finds ways to bring it up whenever possible, . Mr. Allred, 41, played linebacker for the Tennessee Titans before becoming a lawyer. In 2018, he to win his congressional seat in Dallas. "Change can happen quickly in Texas," Mr. Allred, who is Black, said in an interview in which he talked about the diversity of the state. "What we have to do in Texas is embrace who we actually are, which is that diversity and that complexity that comes with it. Instead of being afraid of it." A first debate in the race is scheduled for Oct. 15." " " Colin Allred, Ted Cruz spar over credit for microchip bill," Dallas Morning News'Joseph Morton -- "U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz , R-Texas, and his Democratic challenger, U.S. Rep. Colin Allred of Dallas, agree that Texas can expect new jobs and economic development from a bill easing permitting requirements on new . The two sparred sharply this week, however, over which of them deserves credit for getting the legislation to President Joe Biden 's desk. Allred's camp noted that he . Cruz said he rewrote it in the Senate and convinced House GOP leaders to push his version over the finish line. The dispute comes as the two candidates are locked in a competitive race, with each pitching himself as the best option to deliver on job creation. "A win for Texas! The House passed our bill, the Building Chips in America Act, to streamline permitting and advance CHIPS Act projects," . "Thanks to a team from both sides of the aisle, we got this done." Repeating his criticism that Cruz is more interested in self-promotion than finding solutions, Allred added: "Ted Cruz is trying to claim credit. Classic Ted acting like a 'me guy.' " A prime example, Allred says, was Cruz's vote against the that was intended to boost and is helping bring billions of dollars to new Texas facilities. Cruz says he enthusiastically supported the 2022 bill's tax and regulatory incentives for new manufacturing facilities but strongly objected to its direct corporate subsidies. "I am not a fan of giving taxpayer money directly to private corporations, and I think history has shown that it can lead to bad results," Cruz said. "Once the bill passed, I have actively urged as many of those dollars as possible to go to Texas." Cruz said he was particularly interested in speeding those new manufacturing facilities through a federal environmental review process that can delay projects for years. He recounted seeing an Allred news release announcing the original proposal to ease those requirements. Cruz said some of the original language would have disadvantaged Texas, so he blocked it and asked his staff to write new language. He worked with U.S. Sen. Mark Kelly , D-Ariz., to get that version unanimously approved by the Senate. The reworked bill encountered resistance in the House from some Democrats concerned about undermining environmental regulations and from some Republicans who wanted a more comprehensive overhaul of environmental rules. The House voted 257-125 Monday to approve the Cruz-Kelly version. In an interview, Cruz talked in great detail about the various legislative twists and turns the permitting bill went through on the way to final passage as he lobbied for support in the House and urged House Speaker Mike Johnson , R-La., to bring the bill to the floor. It is "utterly bizarre" that Allred would claim the legislation as his own, he said. "The fact that Colin Allred is trying to claim credit for legislation that I drafted and that I have been fighting a year to pass is emblematic of his campaign," Cruz said. He said Allred is trying to pitch himself as a bipartisan-minded moderate despite voting consistently with his party for years, particularly in opposition to Republican proposals to secure the border and stem illegal immigration." **" Texas' growth at risk due to water shortages, urgent action needed,"** KXAN's**Ryan Chandler** -- "In Wimberley, boulders and deer bones bake in the heat where there was once a thriving creek. The lakes and rivers that once attracted Texans and enabled them to grow communities there are drying up, posing an active but underappreciated emergency that sets a limit on the "Texas Miracle," state leaders say.

"Texas is out of water," Texas Agriculture Commissioner **Sid Miller** told Nexstar on Tuesday. "We can't grow, we can't expand, we can't have economic opportunity and jobs without water. We've reached our limit, there is no more. We've got to do some things different."

Wimberley and much of Central Texas has been in a drought for most of the last two years. It has led some local officials to implement Stage 4 water restrictions, where residents are penalized for automatic water sprinklers and watering is confined to certain times. But out in West Texas, conditions are far worse.

Miller said Texas loses about one farm every week, but it's not for lack of land. Farmers don't have enough water to keep their crops alive.

Texas's population is expected to gain over 22 million people by 2070, according to the 2022 [Texas State Water Plan](https://substack.com/redirect/e13d6266-ae42-4f92-95fa-79efd76ff98e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Over the same period, the water supply is projected to decrease by 18%.

As Texas regularly faces drought periods, some lawmakers are urging the state to proactively protect the most valuable resource.

"It's the silent issue, with the least urgency, with the biggest impact," State Sen. **Charles Perry** , R-Lubbock, previously told Nexstar. "We've been, for far too long, treating water like a commodity that has no meaning. And it's truly not. It's not a commodity. It's a necessity."

Perry, one of the legislature's longtime champions of water conservation, expects it will take billions more.

**" Appeals court says Texas State Fair can ban guns,"** Texas Tribune's **Juan Salinas II** -- "A newly created state appeals court denied Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** request to temporarily block the State Fair of Texas' policy banning all firearms from its fairgrounds as the event is set to start Friday.

Paxton said on social media Tuesday evening that he will next ask the Texas Supreme Court to overturn the ban.

The State Fair begins Friday." [Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/af3491e5-9a83-4165-b60e-ac11717dd442?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

**" Dallas council members request an audit of failed lead abatement program,"** Dallas Morning News' **Maria Ramos Pacheco** -- "Two Dallas council members requested an audit into the $2.3 million failed city's lead removal program after The Dallas Morning News [investigated](https://substack.com/redirect/c7253bc6-8154-4a23-81a2-f50e1e92b461?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its outcome, which left multiple residents exposed to lead.

District 13 Councilmember **Gay Donnell Willis** and District 1 Councilmember **Chad West** sent a memorandum on Sept. 16 to City Auditor **Mark Swann** asking him to add the program to his work plan and examine it more closely.

"The audit should focus on [identifying the causes of program delays,](https://substack.com/redirect/b27ce372-4d38-4747-a34a-9bdc6cc425d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) inefficiencies in executing lead removal, and the lack of contractor availability in Dallas versus other cities where the program has been successful. It should also assess communication with residents and other stakeholders throughout the process," read the memo.

Willis and West did not respond to a request for comment.

_The News_ reached out to **Cynthia Rogers-Ellickson** , interim director of the housing and neighborhood revitalization department, and **Thor Erickson** , the department's assistant director, via email but did not respond to a request for comment.

The city's communication department said via email the managers in the housing department were aware of the audit and would assist the auditor in his review and provide any information requested.

The Office of the City Auditor's Recommended Fiscal Year 2025 Audit Work Plan includes an audit of the lead abatement program. The work plan will be subject to final approval by the full City Council on Oct. 23. After the Work Plan is approved, the audit will be scheduled to start when audit resources are available, said Swann via email." **" While Bexar County barrels toward fiscal 'cliff,' San Antonio sees smoother landing,"** San Antonio Report's **Iris Dimmick** -- "The City of San Antonio put the finishing touches on its [nearly $4 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/d9bedd18-c61a-4463-a2ab-181826cb19f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) fiscal year 2025 budget on Thursday -- and with that, pledged the last scraps of its federal coronavirus pandemic recovery fund.

The city allocated its remaining $5.8 million in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding on one-time expenses, including expanding senior center hours, [relocation assistance](https://substack.com/redirect/2393f1bc-a77f-4540-a3c2-93607a1db3a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for downtown residents and seed funding for a [South Side health equity initiative](https://substack.com/redirect/bb65c2d8-c829-4f7b-a30b-2e1d6c007264?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

Meanwhile, Bexar County adopted a $2.8 billion budget [one week earlier](https://substack.com/redirect/ceb1b78a-c999-49e3-bc75-588597131173?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that sets the county on course toward a so-called "[ARPA cliff](https://substack.com/redirect/1a972045-6012-4eaa-804f-d5a7a8d983a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" unless serious cuts are made or revenue is generated. The county used its last remaining ARPA funds to plug an $18.8 million hole in its general fund budget -- rather than using it for new one-time expenses, as commissioners had previously discussed.

Between the newly established [public health department](https://substack.com/redirect/ac6bb74c-82ef-4225-9c84-9c1ebb495940?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [expanded mental health law enforcement](https://substack.com/redirect/7b853ae9-e8c6-4270-8a57-0104c1d28bc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) program and other initiatives that require reoccurring expenses, the county has bitten off more than its budget can afford in future years without ARPA support.

"How many of those ARPA-funded programs continue in the future" will come down to policy decisions made by the Bexar County Commissioners Court, County Manager **David Smith** said. "As soon as next budget, we're going to have to start examining some of those potential impacts."

The city was careful not to over-extend itself, City Manager **Erik Walsh** said. It ramped up existing programs that it could wind down once funding ran out. The budget deficit that the city had to deal with this year, for the first time since 2010, was due to [slowing revenue growth](https://substack.com/redirect/08e9e2e1-5521-41c9-afd3-3d7ad97b129d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from both property and sales taxes -- not as a result of its dwindling ARPA funds.

"We've planned appropriately for ARPA over the last couple of years and we'll continue to plan for the next year and a half," Walsh said.

"Some cities added firefighters or police officers," he added. "I don't know what the heck they're going to do when that money dries out."" [SA Report](https://substack.com/redirect/b3568b24-437f-4a5e-b96e-0eb3343648b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

**" Fort Worth ISD school board accepts voluntary resignation of Superintendent Angelica Ramsey,"** Fort Worth Report's **Jacob Sanchez** and **Matthew Sgroi** -- "The Angelica Ramsey-led era of Fort Worth ISD is over after the school board accepted her voluntary resignation.

Trustees' 8-1 vote on Sept. 24 came almost to the day two years ago that trustees formally hired Ramsey, who [entered the superintendency with high hopes](https://substack.com/redirect/5f254c07-fd41-4f3a-8b75-1bb9a64f9f26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of improving academic achievement and the district's financial standing. She now leaves the district amid criticism of unchanged student outcomes, a $17.7 million deficit budget and [teachers who say they feel overburdened](https://substack.com/redirect/e73edb97-a401-46b4-8c5f-1bba2d03bbfd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by district mandates.

The sole dissenting vote was trustee **Camille Rodriguez**. The board members came out of a more than three-hour executive session and announced the resignation without comment.

Ramsey's resignation as superintendent is effective Oct. 1, according to a joint statement from the school board and the departing leader. However, she will remain a Fort Worth ISD employee until Aug. 30, 2025.

The school board plans to appoint an interim superintendent. The interim leader will remain in the position as trustees search for a new superintendent.

During a news conference, school board President **Roxanne Martinez** thanked Ramsey for her service and said trustees will move forward with a focus on improving student achievement.

Martinez explained her vote to accept Ramsey's resignation.

"Hearing the community's concerns was a large part of why I supported the decision. I also think we mutually made a decision to move on in the best interest of children," Martinez said. "That's what my focus is going to be as president -- moving forward and improving student achievement just like our community and our parents wish to see."

In a [four-page statement](https://substack.com/redirect/cfb0541f-5d25-4fff-aa23-512726e7641f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Ramsey listed what she saw as her achievements as Fort Worth ISD's superintendent for the past two years, such as improvements seen in the [district's self-assigned A-F ratings](https://substack.com/redirect/a96ec119-2143-41a5-9142-ac3c6673aff2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

"I would like to extend my deepest gratitude to the Fort Worth ISD board for allowing me the honor of serving this district over the past two years. It has been a privilege, and I have approached this responsibility with the utmost seriousness and dedication," Ramsey said."

The pressure put on Ramsey and her leadership had intensified in recent weeks after more than 40 community leaders called for a district turnaround plan. On Aug. 27, in a letter and a [speech to the school board](https://substack.com/redirect/fff59712-4394-4c7e-af2e-0edacd19fd32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Mayor **Mattie Parker** voiced dissatisfaction with the lackluster and stagnant state of the district.

Those critical of Ramsey's tenure also noted empty promises when it came to improving [literacy rates for Black](https://substack.com/redirect/e5d41d2e-7a63-4799-9903-c0a43f6c31d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and Hispanic students. Trustee **Wallace Bridges** voiced his concerns over the district's lack of progress in improving reading rates for Black students during school board meetings. For two years, the district has not had a plan for these students, he said."
