body:
[ https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/67?t=1001&akid=3844%2E35263%2E7T2SmJ ]TAMMY BALDWIN FOR SENATE

Peter — Do you
recognize the little girl in this photo?

[ https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/2155?c0=tbe-em-sep24.J2i10d&refcode=AU_STB_FR_GEN_EOQ_AC_20240926_AM1_V1_S1&t=1004&akid=3844%2E35263%2E7T2SmJ ]Tammy in the hospital when she was young

That’s me. ☝️ Growing up, I was diagnosed with a serious illness and spent
three months in the hospital — where I’m pictured here. When I got better,
my grandparents, who raised me, wanted to make sure I was protected in
case I got sick again.

But they couldn’t find any insurance policies that would cover me in the
future. Not from any insurer. Not at any price.

This meant my grandparents had to make significant sacrifices to pay for
my health care out of pocket — all because I had a pre-existing condition.

It kept my grandparents up late at night, worried that I might fall ill
again and that they wouldn't be able to afford my care. No one should ever
have to go through that.

But I know we were not alone,
Peter, and that our story isn’t
unique. I’m one of 133 million Americans with the label "pre-existing
condition" attached to our care — and before the Affordable Care Act was
passed, many of us could be denied coverage.

That’s why I got into public service.

Now, insurance companies can no longer discriminate against those of us
with a pre-existing condition. I championed health care reform and wrote
the amendment that allows young people to stay on their parents’ insurance
plan until they’re 26 years old. When I meet with young people across
Wisconsin, I’m proud to see almost every hand in the room go up when I ask
who is on their parents’ health insurance.

But let’s be clear: If Eric Hovde flips this seat and Republicans take
back control of the Senate, the ACA will be on the chopping block. He
called my amendment a “stupid idea” and said young people on their
parent’s health insurance need to “grow up and move on.” He’s even said
there’s no part of the ACA he supports.

If we lose this seat and Republicans take back the Senate, countless
Americans could find themselves in a place where insurance companies are
writing the rules once again. That’s why I need your help to protect our
hard-earned progress:

[ https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/2155?c0=tbe-em-sep24.J2i10d&refcode=AU_STB_FR_GEN_EOQ_AC_20240926_AM1_V1_S1&t=1005&akid=3844%2E35263%2E7T2SmJ ]Peter, will
you pitch in to my reelection campaign to help me win this race so we can
protect and expand access to affordable health care? I’ve stood up against
Republicans’ efforts to repeal the ACA before, and it’s going to take a
team of powerful grassroots supporters to help us win this fight.

But I know we were not alone, Peter, and that our story isn’t unique. I’m one of 133 million Americans with the label "pre-existing condition" attached to our care — and before the Affordable Care Act was passed, many of us could be denied coverage. That’s why I got into public service. Now, insurance companies can no longer discriminate against those of us with a pre-existing condition. I championed health care reform and wrote the amendment that allows young people to stay on their parents’ insurance plan until they’re 26 years old. When I meet with young people across Wisconsin, I’m proud to see almost every hand in the room go up when I ask who is on their parents’ health insurance. But let’s be clear: If Eric Hovde flips this seat and Republicans take back control of the Senate, the ACA will be on the chopping block. He called my amendment a “stupid idea” and said young people on their parent’s health insurance need to “grow up and move on.” He’s even said there’s no part of the ACA he supports. If we lose this seat and Republicans take back the Senate, countless Americans could find themselves in a place where insurance companies are writing the rules once again. That’s why I need your help to protect our hard-earned progress: [ ]Peter, will you pitch in to my reelection campaign to help me win this race so we can protect and expand access to affordable health care? I’ve stood up against Republicans’ efforts to repeal the ACA before, and it’s going to take a team of powerful grassroots supporters to help us win this fight. Dear Friend,

Politics often leaves a bitter taste in our mouths. It's no wonder so many of us approach it with disdain. The endless mudslinging, pandering to special interest groups, and policies shaped by poll numbers rather than deeply held convictions make politics seem like a world Christians should avoid.

Yet, as Christians, we can't ignore the rapid unraveling of our culture or remain passive in the face of the evil we see around us. The Bible tells us that our citizenship is in heaven (Philippians 3:20) and that we are aliens and strangers in this world (1 Peter 2:11). But does that mean we should leave governing to unbelievers? Should we invest our time in influencing what seems transitory at best?

The answer is simple: Jesus commanded us to be the salt and light of the world (Matthew 5:13-14). As Christians, we are called to preserve the spiritual and moral fabric of society wherever God has placed us. And that includes influencing every aspect of our culture--entertainment, business, education, and yes, even government.
---
| | As the upcoming election approaches, how should we allow the Bible to guide our decisions? In my new 44-page booklet, _How a Christian Should Vote_ , I offer a biblical framework for assessing candidates, their faith, policies, and constitutional views. This practical resource will help you view the election from a biblical perspective, equipping you to make informed decisions.
---
| [](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/u/click?_t=29bc9815846f49728b1d374165de7bf2&_m=59a0a83580ad4884a8a950feee15ee8c&_e=FaTSZi_A0Qc_SPHJUf-mD1dhzFKkNQoyHStVN6d897ueBOMt14l5VUmSLevaSH4erVLHWFN2n40fZX_gRu2PK5DKWNKH_7LIMCMQyyZ945kLlROANWbOeKTUWJu2zQ3PxG1wh7Xfs46n8cEQgb-WbMm8hRRtPV2b3emVpV3cZjzpvP0h3TLXMIyPHQfMWUqh7H-uyB7QCEOKm9hv_eABU3RFeK7jTGs_lVcCv-bt_BT3BoNPYnKM1fGPX1CWo7jim7zgzgj_ITSVHvrSokJmHaGagdSNvPsRHtPGszDDifhmgdTy2ye0HNHso9KEjh__tvlNJTusITEFk6L7tZXwHa_6C-mrYwWQEZVNVSDWHR992n8Q9irMue6KA_Q2csKP7tMkXOJJAHdYuj4dHBIo-g%3D%3D)

| | There are 4 main questions that a Christian should be asking themselves before casting a vote: Is the candidate a Christian?
Do the candidate's policies align with the Bible?
What is the candidate's view of Israel?
Will the candidate get things done?

You can receive a free copy of _How a Christian Should Vote_ in time for the elections by clicking here: [https://ptv.org/nna/how-a-christian-should-vote-by-dr-robert-jeffress-2024/](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/u/click?_t=29bc9815846f49728b1d374165de7bf2&_m=59a0a83580ad4884a8a950feee15ee8c&_e=FaTSZi_A0Qc_SPHJUf-mD1dhzFKkNQoyHStVN6d897ueBOMt14l5VUmSLevaSH4erVLHWFN2n40fZX_gRu2PK5DKWNKH_7LIMCMQyyZ945kLlROANWbOeKTUWJu2zQ3PxG1wh7Xfs46n8cEQgb-WbMm8hRRtPV2b3emVpV3cZjzpvP0h3TLXMIyPHQfMWUqh7H-uyB7QCEOKm9hv_eABU3RFeK7jTGs_lVcCv-bt_BT3BoNPYnKM1fGPX1CWo7jibMCMjYSrl2824VTUE14zmYtIsn-1ayFK6L4JXYkU0WeuCjZcjdGBpUqvNumZqug0kbPbunS7MYb5AmkzYPsXOgPzONBtKijzpd-e5Tfrau-83ZiW_HclPoqB0_viFwDOXQTVivZYSrVD8NFP-Fk56Q%3D%3D)

Together, we can determine the direction of our country by voting for leaders who will embrace principles that bring God's favor upon our nation.

In Christ,

Dr. Robert Jeffress

| **ABOUT NELLA**
**New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years.

Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant.

Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans.

Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. **

AP: Federal appeals court deals a blow to Voting Rights Act, ruling that private plaintiffs can’t sue [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=092624_2&amount=25]
The recent 8th Circuit ruling is one of the most dangerous anti-voter rulings we’ve seen in years . In the eight states impacted by the ruling, voters and voting rights organizations can no longer sue to overturn unjust laws under the Voting Rights Act.
In plain language -- pro-voting lawsuits brought in states like Wisconsin, Georgia, Florida, and others nationwide wouldn't be possible anymore if the Supreme Court backs up this ruling and gets rid of the "private right of action".
We won’t sugarcoat this: That ruling could be a crushing blow to many voting rights organizations, including Voter Action Project. If this ruling is not overturned by a higher court, it could unravel all of the great work organizations like ours are doing across the country — and allow dozens of unjust, unconstitutional voter restrictions to stand.
This attack on the Voting Rights Act highlights the importance of the other work we’ll do over the next year, as well: Voter registration, education, mobilization and more. As voter suppression laws become increasingly targeted and oppressive , our work to combat them must become smarter, stronger and more accessible to everyone.
Team, we have to fight harder than ever to protect the right to vote in 2024. Please pitch in $25 or whatever you can to stand with us in a crucial moment >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=092624_2&amount=25]

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: Abolish the filibuster
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
It’s simple: We either protect the filibuster or we protect our rights.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20240926-4334-footer&t=1&akid=4334%2E420207%2Eg4QNCv)
Peter,
We all know there’s a lot at stake in this election. But this week, we got a really positive indication of just how much progress we’ll be able to make if we succeed in flipping the House, holding the Senate, and electing Kamala Harris and Tim Walz this November.
**That’s because Kamala Harris just came out in favor of eliminating the Senate filibuster for reproductive rights** , alongside key Democratic senators like Bob Casey from Pennsylvania. That’s HUGE!
[**Will you pitch in $3 toward our end-of-quarter goal so we can meet this moment and keep our people-powered movement strong as Election Day approaches?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-20240926-1?refcode=em20240926-1&amount=3&refcode2=4334_420207_g4QNCv&akid=4334%2E420207%2Eg4QNCv)
**[Contribute](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-20240926-1?amount=3&refcode=em20240926-1-4334&refcode2=4334_420207_g4QNCv&akid=4334%2E420207%2Eg4QNCv)**
Time and time in the past, voters have delivered Democrats the White House, House, and Senate on the expectation that we’ll deliver for the people in a big way. And on far too many of those occasions, the filibuster has killed any hope of real progress.
**It’s simple: We either protect the filibuster or we protect our rights.** If we win this November, we can’t afford to squander the opportunity we’ll have by allowing Senate Republicans like Mitch McConnell and Ted Cruz to filibuster bills on reproductive rights and so many other important issues.
But while I couldn’t be happier to see support growing for abolishing the filibuster, the reality is we still have an election to win before we get to that point. And right now, we’re coming up on our final FEC-mandated fundraising deadline before Election Day.
**Our $34,000 end-of-quarter goal wasn’t made up out of thin air.** It’s the number we need to reach if we want to keep funding all the organizing and outreach work we’re doing both here in Washington _and_ in swing states across the country. And since I don’t take corporate PAC money, I’m counting on your support to reach it.
**Peter, if you’re ready to elect Kamala Harris, Tim Walz, and Democrats across the country who are ready to deliver real progressive change, including by abolishing the filibuster,[then will you pitch in $3 before Monday’s deadline to help us reach our goal?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-20240926-1?refcode=em20240926-1&amount=3&refcode2=4334_420207_g4QNCv&akid=4334%2E420207%2Eg4QNCv)**
**[Contribute](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-20240926-1?amount=3&refcode=em20240926-1-4334&refcode2=4334_420207_g4QNCv&akid=4334%2E420207%2Eg4QNCv)**
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal
**[Contribute](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-footer?refcode=em20240926-4334-footer&t=2&refcode2=4334_420207_g4QNCv&akid=4334%2E420207%2Eg4QNCv)**

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way we keep in touch with people like you, and small-dollar contributions sustain our movement for transformative change. To contribute by check, please address to Pramila for Congress, PO Box 21912, Seattle, WA 98111.

subject: Before it’s too late
body:
But please don't stop reading -- because God-fearing, faith-filled people like you and me have a job to do today.

| | Dear Fellow Conservative,
---
| | I'm writing to ask you to stand beside me at the top of a very slippery slope.Actually, in my case, it's a slippery _slide_. My name is Riley Gaines and I'm the University of Kentucky swimmer who had to compete against a fully intact 6'4" _male_ swimmer dressed in a women's bathing suit.And after he stole the victory I had worked for my entire life, I had to go back to the women's locker room and undress out of my wet bathing suit while he did the same next to me.
---
| [](https://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/8jf8yEwt9TpyvHLOOKXSVQ~~/AARclAA~~)
---
| | I know the images I'm bringing up are horrible. But please don't stop reading -- because God-fearing, faith-filled people like you and me have a job to do today. We can't retreat into our homes and hope our government's evil culture just passes us by. **[That's why I'm asking you to stand with me today -- before it's too late.](https://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/8jf8yEwt9TpyvHLOOKXSVQ~~/AARclAA~~)** My fellow conservative, you know this slippery slide.It's the same one you got pushed down when the Left told you abortion was going to be "safe, legal, and rare."_Now abortion is a "right" and "women’s healthcare." And if you don’t support it up until the moment of birth, you must "hate women."_ It's the same slippery slide you got pushed down when the Left told you limiting gay couples to civil unions was "mean." You were told, "They just want to use the word "marriage" like everyone else. It's just a word."_Now if you don't fully embrace a homosexual lifestyle by displaying rainbows and celebrating gay pride, you're a "hate-filled bigot."_ Enough with their lies. We have Truth on our side. And we need to start acting like it.**God created man. And God created woman. It isn't any more complicated than that.** Letting men believe they are women... letting girls believe they are boys... is a bold-faced rejection of God’s truth. And if we give this deranged movement one more inch, a year from now when you're forced by law to call boys "she"... when it becomes normal for kids to be taken away from parents who oppose this evil... I don't want you looking back with regret wishing you had done something when you still had a chance.**Your chance is right now -- and right by my side.** **[Please stand with me against the radical transgender movement by making an urgent tax-deductible donation today -- before it's too late.](https://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/8jf8yEwt9TpyvHLOOKXSVQ~~/AARclAA~~) **The radical transgender movement has parents backed into a corner. But when I'm speaking around the country, I meet so many seniors who say, "I wish someone had told me about this sooner." The good news is that right now, you still have a chance to help me stop the radical transgender movement before they push us down their slippery slide.And today I'm writing you on behalf of a group that is doing more work to block the transgender movement than anyone I know. **It's the legal non-profit the Center for American Liberty.** **[And your tax-deductible gift today is going straight to help them.](https://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/8jf8yEwt9TpyvHLOOKXSVQ~~/AARclAA~~)** With the help of patriots like you, the _Center for American Liberty_ fights the transgender movement _in the courts_ because that’s the only way to stop them. And the _Center for American Liberty_ is attacking this evil from all sides with their comprehensive three-pronged approach.
---
**#1. They're fighting radical schools**.
---
---
**#2. They're fighting radical doctors.**
---
---
**#3. They're fighting for _your_ right to speak out against this evil.**
---
**[**When you make your tax-deductible gift today**](https://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/8jf8yEwt9TpyvHLOOKXSVQ~~/AARclAA~~)** , you're helping the _Center for American Liberty_ protect every American's right to speak out against this evil! I know you'd probably love to fund an entire court case on your own after all I've told you.**[But all I'm asking you to do is make a tax-deductible gift of $25, $50, $75, $100 or even $250 or more today -- before it's too late.](https://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/8jf8yEwt9TpyvHLOOKXSVQ~~/AARclAA~~)** Please donate whatever amount is right for you whether it's smaller or larger. _The Center for American Liberty_ needs and appreciates every dollar that comes in.And because I believe so strongly in the work they're doing -- and because they are one of the few groups who've stood shoulder-to-shoulder with me in this fight... I**t will be my honor to send you my new book _Swimming Against the Current: Fighting for Common Sense in a World That's Lost Its Mind_ as my free gift** **[**when you donate $100 or more to the Center for American Liberty.**](https://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/8jf8yEwt9TpyvHLOOKXSVQ~~/AARclAA~~)** Before I go, please let me share one last thought with you.Every morning as a competitive swimmer, I would get up and think of this verse: _For I consider that the sufferings of the present time are not worthy to be compared to the glory that is about to be revealed to us. Romans 8:18_ I applied it to my swimming: work hard now and wins come later. But now I see that God has a much bigger plan for my life just as He does for yours.Thank you for reading my letter all the way to the end. I'm praying for you, and I hope you'll pray for me too.
---
Sincerely,
---
| | Riley Gaines

The attempts to deny those basic truths, are attempts to deny the truth of God. Your help is so critical to the _Center for American Liberty's_ work, **[when you donate $100 or more, as my personal "Thank You," I'll send you my new book,_Swimming Against the Current: Fighting for Common Sense in a World That's Lost Its Mind_ for free.](https://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/8jf8yEwt9TpyvHLOOKXSVQ~~/AARclAA~~)** Please hurry. It's the same slippery slide you got pushed down when the Left told you limiting gay couples to civil unions was "mean." You were told, "They just want to use the word "marriage" like everyone else. It's just a word."Now if you don't fully embrace a homosexual lifestyle by displaying rainbows and celebrating gay pride, you're a "hate-filled bigot." Enough with their lies. We have Truth on our side. And we need to start acting like it.God created man. And God created woman. It isn't any more complicated than that. Letting men believe they are women... letting girls believe they are boys... is a bold-faced rejection of God’s truth. And if we give this deranged movement one more inch, a year from now when you're forced by law to call boys "she"... when it becomes normal for kids to be taken away from parents who oppose this evil... I don't want you looking back with regret wishing you had done something when you still had a chance.Your chance is right now -- and right by my side. ~ The radical transgender movement has parents backed into a corner. But when I'm speaking around the country, I meet so many seniors who say, "I wish someone had told me about this sooner." The good news is that right now, you still have a chance to help me stop the radical transgender movement before they push us down their slippery slide.And today I'm writing you on behalf of a group that is doing more work to block the transgender movement than anyone I know. I'm about to ask you to **[make a $10 donation ahead of my upcoming final end-of-quarter deadline before Election Day.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/93646261/501154869/-862660935?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&amount=10&refcode=jtk5446-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTkvMS83MjcyMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiNjI0OWExZS0zODdjLWVmMTEtODQ3My02MDQ1YmRhOGFhMzQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=dNTy_AeRjyJhJTFitxy-E6EwrdooVLx0AyvBxGzMUbk=) **This is an incredibly important deadline, and I'm counting on your help to hit my goal. **But first, I want to thank you — so much — for supporting my campaign.**
I'm fighting every single day to earn your support and deliver on the promises I've made to you. From certifying the Equal Rights Amendment so that we can restore reproductive rights nationwide to fighting gun violence and keeping our communities safe, I'm working tirelessly to win change for your family.
As my grandmother taught me when I was a young girl, politics isn't about parties or polling numbers._ It's about the people._ It's my job to serve your family and do everything that I can to make life better for __you__. And it's an honor that I'm grateful for every day. So thank you for trusting me with your support and giving me this incredible opportunity to serve.
I wish that I could end this email here. But unfortunately, elections are an unavoidable part of politics. And to continue to serve your family in the Senate and win progress on all the issues you care about — reproductive rights, affordable health care, protecting our seniors and so much more — **I need your help.**
Democrats are heading into a historically difficult election cycle. And here in New York, right-wing extremists had their best election in decades in 2022. I'm confident that we can reverse that trend this year. **But because I refuse to accept money from corporate PACs, I'm counting on grassroots donations to compete with far-right megadonors.**

name: No Dem Left Behind
subject: Across the Country: September 26th, 2024
body:
MAGA prioritizes profits over people in Tennessee.
| | | | | |
---
**_Across the Country_**
---
|
---
Hello, folks! Welcome back to _Across the Country_ , our weekly series at No Dem Left Behind! We’re diving into the most pressing issues impacting the heartland of America as the 2024 election approaches. These are the stories that actually matter to our communities. Let’s stay informed, together. –Daniela Rodriguez
---
| | | | **Tennessee**
---
|
---
Elon Musk's new AI data center in Memphis is raising serious alarms among residents and environmentalists. Locals worry about the impact the new center will have on the community. It will be considered the "largest AI data center on the planet," the facility threatens local air and water quality, drawing vast amounts of energy and water from a region that already struggles with pollution and health. Community members feel exploited by Musk's corporate practices that prioritize profit over their well-being. With little transparency regarding the project's implications, residents fear that the data center will exacerbate existing environmental challenges and health risks. There’s an urgent need for ethical economic development that genuinely benefits all people and puts locals first. Environmental racism has been a long time issue in America. Vulnerable communities like Memphis, face health concerns that are repeatedly disregarded by big corporations who continue to pollute and contaminate predominantly Black and Brown communities. The Pew Research Center has recorded that 70% of Americans support U.S. participation in International efforts to combat climate change; yet, there are still major enablers and powerful actors actively reversing climate action efforts despite public opinion. Memphis has endured a long list of health and environmental concerns. In 2022, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) paid a visit to locals, informing them that Sterilization Services of Tennessee had been emitting a dangerous amount of toxins like ethylene oxide, a gas used to sterilize medical equipment since the 1970’s, and has likely been a large contributor to health risks in the area. Memphis is currently being exposed to 7 different cancer causing air toxins, placing it in the 95th percentile of cancer risks in comparison to the rest of Tennessee.
---
|
---
Locals have been resilient to environmental racism for way too long; it’s time to put Memphis and other exposed and exploited communities at the forefront of this election. Memphis stands empowered as activists band together to stop these unregulated corporations from raising the percentage of deaths and cancer. This is when our individual votes count the most. Including DC, Tennessee ranks 51st in voter turnout, meaning it’s the state with **THE LOWEST VOTER TURNOUT.** Pew Research Center polling shows that 42.6% of adults in Tennessee identify as Republican, and 43% lean Democrat, meaning if more people showed up to the polls and voted, Tennessee would be facing a very different reality. This isn’t even including moderates with no political lean! There’s never been a more pressing time for Tennesseans to come together, register to vote, and show up to the polls. Because we know that when we unite in the fight for the heartland of America, we win! **Join us next week with Sabrina for the latest updates on nationwide breaking news. Make sure to stay informed with NDLB!**
---
|
---
-Daniela Rodriguez
---
| | | | |
---
**No Dem Left Behind PAC** P.O. Box 15320 Washington, D.C. 20003
---

Happy World Contraception Day, Friend!
When it comes to reproductive healthcare decisions, the difference between Democrats and extremist Republicans could not be clearer. Chip in to support Democrats this November >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/srodriguez-email?refcode=20240926_em_fr_b1_SR_NGP]
Republicans say they support access to contraceptives, but they refuse to pass anything to protect them.
When abortion protections were struck down by Dobbs , attacks on procedures like IVF and access to contraceptives became far scarier. Republicans have attempted to assure Americans that they do not support a ban on contraceptives.
But they repeatedly fail to act on the issue. When Democrats in the Wisconsin State Legislature introduced a right-to-contraception bill, Republicans didn't just vote it down—they refused to hold a vote at all .
Friend, the Republican majority in our state legislature has resisted our attempts to codify contraceptive access.
That means that the only way to guarantee our rights are protected is to take away their majority.
I'm working to elect champions of our health, our schools, and our freedoms down ballot across Wisconsin this November. Can you help me do that with a contribution today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/srodriguez-email?refcode=20240926_em_fr_b1_SR_NGP]

In service,
Lt. Gov Sara Rodriguez
Lt. Gov. Sara Rodriguez, MSN, MPH, RN, was sworn in as Wisconsin’s 46th Lieutenant Governor on January 3, 2023. A working mom, wife, and proud Wisconsinite, Lt. Gov. Rodriguez was elected on November 8, 2022. Before her election, she served in the Wisconsin State Assembly, representing Assembly District 13, comprising a portion of Waukesha and Milwaukee Counties. While serving as a state representative, she worked on the Committees on Health, Insurance, Energy and Utilities, and Science, Technology and Broadband.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/srodriguez-email?refcode=20240926_em_fr_b1_SR_NGP [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/srodriguez-email?refcode=20240926_em_fr_b1_SR_NGP]
Lt. Gov. Rodriguez is an experienced healthcare executive who has worked in various leadership roles for over 20 years, including founding her own small business. Prior to serving in the Wisconsin State Assembly, Lt. Gov. Rodriguez was the vice president of Population Health and Integrated Care Management at one of the largest healthcare systems in the Midwest. In this role, she provided strategic direction to the teams that managed population health interventions for risk-based contracts and direct-to-employer products.
Before running for office, Lt. Gov. Rodriguez built a career in public health and population health management. She held positions with public health departments at the local, state, and federal levels, including serving as an epidemic intelligence service officer with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the chronic disease director for the state of Colorado, a healthcare systems consultant, and a vice president at a Fortune 100 Company.

subject: Dr Garcia is Reaching Out to Swing Voters
body:
Your Donations are Keeping Our Ads on the Air! | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/garciaforwa/weeklyupdate09262024?e=3ed3552a03)
---
|

[](https://garciaforwa.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe0c756dc01af594bb0bab517&id=3b5cd82f14&e=3ed3552a03)
|
---
|
---
|
# Dr Garcia’s Path to Victory: Swing Voters in WA who Want Change
---
| “How can you win in Washington state?” It’s a question we hear a lot, and it’s a fair one. The fact is, Dr Garcia wouldn’t be in this race if he didn’t think he could win!
There is a path to victory for Dr Garcia and the other Republican candidates who are focused not on partisan politics, but on solving the problems facing the people of Washington.
---
| | | | | | | | | |
---
|
---
| _Dr Garcia at the Apple Cup_
---
| Polling shows that swing voters — persuadable Democrats as well as independents — are sick and tired of the extreme partisanship at all levels of government, and are very concerned about problems such as the fentanyl crisis, rising crime, the high cost of living, access to healthcare, and more.
What’s more, a big chunk of swing voters who think our state & country are on the wrong track, and who want a change from career politicians like Sen. Maria Cantwell, didn’t vote in the primary election but will vote in the general election. Their votes can give Dr Garcia enough of a margin to put him over the top in November.
Dr Garcia’s focus on issues important to swing & independent voters — especially on solving the fentanyl crisis — gives him an edge. Additionally, starting at the beginning of September he’s been spending the majority of his time in Seattle so he can meet as many Puget Sound area voters as possible.
Finally, we’ve been running ads specifically targeted to swing voters. Last week we shared with you [our new ad](https://garciaforwa.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe0c756dc01af594bb0bab517&id=d43cdf9868&e=3ed3552a03) featuring a lifelong Democrat who is supporting Dr Garcia because of his stance on aggressively & effectively fighting the fentanyl crisis:
---
[](https://garciaforwa.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe0c756dc01af594bb0bab517&id=314aa9ca1a&e=3ed3552a03)
|
---
|
# Your Donations Keep Our Ads Running!
---
| A big thank you to everyone who answered our call for donations! [Your support](https://garciaforwa.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe0c756dc01af594bb0bab517&id=2002c0e96a&e=3ed3552a03) is going directly to our video and display ads which are now running on digital & streaming platforms.
If you’re able to give, or give more, you’ll make sure our voter outreach efforts — such as the ad above — keep going strong all the way to Election Day.
[Your donation of $5, $10, $25, $50, $75, $100, or whatever you can give, is crucial to defeating Sen. Maria Cantwell and bringing Dr Garcia’s new leadership to Washington state.](https://garciaforwa.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe0c756dc01af594bb0bab517&id=449d4a878d&e=3ed3552a03)
[Click here](https://garciaforwa.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe0c756dc01af594bb0bab517&id=42c01c0f7f&e=3ed3552a03) to make a secure online contribution, or on the Donate button below.
---
[DONATE TODAY](https://garciaforwa.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe0c756dc01af594bb0bab517&id=7afd968a04&e=3ed3552a03)
| Thank you for your support!
---
|
---
|
# Dr Garcia on Spanish Language TV
---
| Raul is currently in Miami, where he grew up after escaping communist Cuba with his mother at age 11, fundraising and drumming up support for his campaign among the Cuban & Latino communities. When elected, Dr Garcia will be the first Latino to hold statewide office in Washington state!
Yesterday [Raul was interviewed on America TeVe Miami](https://garciaforwa.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe0c756dc01af594bb0bab517&id=3d7894684c&e=3ed3552a03), which reaches Spanish-speaking audiences across the country — including Washington. The interview is in Spanish — if you don’t speak the language you can activate English subtitles on YouTube:

# **RITE files amicus in Montana case on Election Day voter registration**
#
(Washington, DC – September 26, 2024) - Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections (RITE), a non-profit organization that supports litigation to protect election security and integrity, today [filed an amicus curiae, or “friend of the court” brief, with the U.S. Supreme Court](https://riteusa.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc5917dfc5aa19cc3795efbb2&id=6602fb3b32&e=ea91f782ea) in a Montana case regarding the right of the state legislature to regulate state elections.

At issue is a Montana Supreme Court decision that disabled the state’s legislature from moving the deadline to register to vote from the close of polls on election day to noon the day before election day. The court issued this ruling even though the state’s constitution grants the legislature unfettered discretion to allow, or disallow, election-day registration. RITE’s brief argues that this is impermissible judicial lawmaking, precisely the type of conduct the Supreme Court said just last year is incompatible with the federal Constitution.

RITE President Derek Lyons issued the following statement:

“The U.S. Supreme Court correctly ruled last year that state supreme courts must be deferential to election rules enacted by state legislatures. But here, the Montana Supreme Court concluded that the legislature violated the right to vote by foreclosing citizens’ ability to register at the polls on election day. And it did so, despite the fact that the Montana Constitution expressly disclaims the existence of any right to register on election day. The Supreme Court has made it clear that state supreme courts must respect the will of the people, as reflected in the legislative enactments of their elected representatives. This case gives the Court a chance to show that it was serious about ensuring that legislatures, not courts, are in charge of our elections.”

# ###

| **ABOUT NELLA**
**New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years.

Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant.

Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans.

Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. **

**" Gerald Goines found guilty of felony murder in Harding Street deaths,"** Houston Chronicle's**Nicole Hensley** -- "A jury convicted **Gerald Goines**, the former Houston police officer behind the [deadly Harding Street raid](https://substack.com/redirect/008590f6-0f39-4b2f-b253-b59ec7787d79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), of felony murder Wednesday in the 2019 deaths of **Dennis Tuttle** and his wife, **Rhogena Nicholas** , cementing the retiree as a rare example of a law enforcement official in Texas and nationwide facing criminal repercussions for an on-duty killing.

Tuttle's family hurried into a witness room to embrace each other after the jury delivered its verdict.

Goines, 59, bowed his head after the verdict was read. He was taken into custody as one of his defense attorneys, **Mac Secrest** , exchanged heated words with a bailiff, uttering at least one profanity and expressing worry that the exiting jury could see the deputies surrounding his newly-convicted client.

Another deputy placed his hand on Secrest's arm as Goines was guided to a holdover room for inmates. Goines was then booked into the 1200 Baker jail facility, records show.

The judge ordered the jury, who deliberated for nearly eight hours, to return Thursday and hear testimony from those with allegations of additional misconduct to guide how to punish the former officer, as a felony murder charge carries anywhere from five years to life in prison. Records show prosecutors had requested that multiple people once imprisoned following their arrest by Goines appear at trial. Some of those cases have been overturned after authorities scrutinized Goines' arrests.

Goines coincidentally arrested former Houston resident **George Floyd** for selling a small amount of drugs in 2004, years before his 2020 murder at the hands of a Minneapolis police officer. Floyd pleaded guilty to a drug charge and was sentenced to 10 months in a state jail.

The defense may bring forward witnesses to urge the jury to show leniency toward Goines.

The jury's verdict comes more than two weeks after the start of testimony in the closely watched criminal case, slammed by Goines' lawyers and other defense observers as politically charged and a step too far. The testimony ranged from police officers tasked with surrounding the Harding Street home as the raid unfolded to a former officer who is awaiting sentencing on charges related to the raid. Jurors reviewed evidence that showed Goines fabricated a confidential informant who bought heroin from the Pecan Park home, which he then used to secure a judge's approval to enter the home.

* **TOP NEWS**

**" Gerald Goines found guilty of felony murder in Harding Street deaths,"** Houston Chronicle's**Nicole Hensley** -- "A jury convicted **Gerald Goines**, the former Houston police officer behind the [deadly Harding Street raid](https://substack.com/redirect/20572dcc-ac75-41e1-ad1d-465ce46a98a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), of felony murder Wednesday in the 2019 deaths of **Dennis Tuttle** and his wife, **Rhogena Nicholas** , cementing the retiree as a rare example of a law enforcement official in Texas and nationwide facing criminal repercussions for an on-duty killing.

Tuttle's family hurried into a witness room to embrace each other after the jury delivered its verdict.

Goines, 59, bowed his head after the verdict was read. He was taken into custody as one of his defense attorneys, **Mac Secrest** , exchanged heated words with a bailiff, uttering at least one profanity and expressing worry that the exiting jury could see the deputies surrounding his newly-convicted client.

Another deputy placed his hand on Secrest's arm as Goines was guided to a holdover room for inmates. Goines was then booked into the 1200 Baker jail facility, records show.

The judge ordered the jury, who deliberated for nearly eight hours, to return Thursday and hear testimony from those with allegations of additional misconduct to guide how to punish the former officer, as a felony murder charge carries anywhere from five years to life in prison. Records show prosecutors had requested that multiple people once imprisoned following their arrest by Goines appear at trial. Some of those cases have been overturned after authorities scrutinized Goines' arrests.

Goines coincidentally arrested former Houston resident **George Floyd** for selling a small amount of drugs in 2004, years before his 2020 murder at the hands of a Minneapolis police officer. Floyd pleaded guilty to a drug charge and was sentenced to 10 months in a state jail.

The defense may bring forward witnesses to urge the jury to show leniency toward Goines.

The jury's verdict comes more than two weeks after the start of testimony in the closely watched criminal case, slammed by Goines' lawyers and other defense observers as politically charged and a step too far. The testimony ranged from police officers tasked with surrounding the Harding Street home as the raid unfolded to a former officer who is awaiting sentencing on charges related to the raid. Jurors reviewed evidence that showed Goines fabricated a confidential informant who bought heroin from the Pecan Park home, which he then used to secure a judge's approval to enter the home.

Many officers said they would not have participated in the raid had they known about Goines' falsehoods.

The defense conceded that while Goines lied about the use of a confidential informant in the Harding Street raid, they asserted a murder charge was not merited." ($5/mo or $50/yr or $199 lifetime) TOP NEWS " Gerald Goines found guilty of felony murder in Harding Street deaths," Houston Chronicle'sNicole Hensley -- "A jury convicted Gerald Goines, the former Houston police officer behind the , of felony murder Wednesday in the 2019 deaths of Dennis Tuttle and his wife, Rhogena Nicholas , cementing the retiree as a rare example of a law enforcement official in Texas and nationwide facing criminal repercussions for an on-duty killing. Tuttle's family hurried into a witness room to embrace each other after the jury delivered its verdict. Goines, 59, bowed his head after the verdict was read. He was taken into custody as one of his defense attorneys, Mac Secrest , exchanged heated words with a bailiff, uttering at least one profanity and expressing worry that the exiting jury could see the deputies surrounding his newly-convicted client. Another deputy placed his hand on Secrest's arm as Goines was guided to a holdover room for inmates. Goines was then booked into the 1200 Baker jail facility, records show. The judge ordered the jury, who deliberated for nearly eight hours, to return Thursday and hear testimony from those with allegations of additional misconduct to guide how to punish the former officer, as a felony murder charge carries anywhere from five years to life in prison. Records show prosecutors had requested that multiple people once imprisoned following their arrest by Goines appear at trial. Some of those cases have been overturned after authorities scrutinized Goines' arrests. Goines coincidentally arrested former Houston resident George Floyd for selling a small amount of drugs in 2004, years before his 2020 murder at the hands of a Minneapolis police officer. Floyd pleaded guilty to a drug charge and was sentenced to 10 months in a state jail. The defense may bring forward witnesses to urge the jury to show leniency toward Goines. The jury's verdict comes more than two weeks after the start of testimony in the closely watched criminal case, slammed by Goines' lawyers and other defense observers as politically charged and a step too far. The testimony ranged from police officers tasked with surrounding the Harding Street home as the raid unfolded to a former officer who is awaiting sentencing on charges related to the raid. Jurors reviewed evidence that showed Goines fabricated a confidential informant who bought heroin from the Pecan Park home, which he then used to secure a judge's approval to enter the home. Many officers said they would not have participated in the raid had they known about Goines' falsehoods. The defense conceded that while Goines lied about the use of a confidential informant in the Harding Street raid, they asserted a murder charge was not merited." Peter - Voting is no longer just on the first Tuesday in November.

With the rise of early and absentee voting, we can't get swamped by Democrats because we are unprepared.

**_Four more years of Democrats in control of the Senate would be a disaster for America._**
That's why we're focused on getting as many Republicans as possible to vote early or absentee.

| | Dear Fellow American,

I'm glad you opened my email today! I have something urgent to ask you that will shape the future of our families, communities, and country.

[**Will you take our National Opinion Survey on Critical Race Theory (CRT)?**](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/u/click?_t=5b1853ae48754bee8f471363fe4933a9&_m=01c94548b1594d43be118a65afd9d7ac&_e=ToX9KSIMXbtn108n-R4Ns5Jn-EgAnZtwr-eNKnkJXhZB33mIMsdiqJwaUj0e-vDLvL15veJ3lMos1c5oBiVj4HMMR-dD0iVfZcno8Bek1q-InQlEmiY0FZwKLKAn9fPttXqCq0zfNogs4DPyDMdvV_A9Ahl85Z6Tg5aAeWrhW08TXh_B5z_EpaDhn-jn2Fxnu8hsiTwK0O9dyki-zV60a0jQa7aGYbiJxO9nvl29J9ymLi5MSzPemAu8NIes4A-15CMZzz00aYhxi2E2Y58MKYm3ILWaLmn_vl3mksCtvKwsaEX9X-0hV2aFmFfTy5qRcrgSRpFtMfOwm5EWwWwWsryQ1ni4orNOz42Et0eNvpuX8YqAKfQBvb-NKY3HSUr_)

Your participation will help us understand and address many Americans' concerns about CRT's influence on our society.

This survey will only take just a few minutes.

But in those few minutes, you'll help us gather important insights to defend America's founding principles of liberty...

...and ensure a bright future for our children and grandchildren.

**You can share your thoughts on CRT in the National Opinion Survey on Critical Race Theory Survey here:**

[**https://info.hillsdale.edu/crt-survey/**](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/u/click?_t=5b1853ae48754bee8f471363fe4933a9&_m=01c94548b1594d43be118a65afd9d7ac&_e=ToX9KSIMXbtn108n-R4Ns5Jn-EgAnZtwr-eNKnkJXhZB33mIMsdiqJwaUj0e-vDLvL15veJ3lMos1c5oBiVj4HMMR-dD0iVfZcno8Bek1q-InQlEmiY0FZwKLKAn9fPttXqCq0zfNogs4DPyDMdvV_A9Ahl85Z6Tg5aAeWrhW08TXh_B5z_EpaDhn-jn2Fxnu8hsiTwK0O9dyki-zV60a1_5PM7BSWDUlwY5aIFwubWpgb7IPqUvvQpozBIh_E4nAEPSdeNc9qWgtFwrvh1J3tODS50qmTEspfhMEPwzpHZyW2nWR3qLw3bXmY0KMJ0f9XrOPnT56h9vGgEw7cfwDESydpLiQvR8DO9bpXY5RAxqDKZA3Ym3j9hs0nbngV4Y)

Sharing your opinion is an important way you'll combat the spread of CRT in our schools and workplaces. Together, we can preserve the constitutional and free-enterprise principles that made our nation so great and so free.

Thanks in advance! I look forward to seeing your response.

Bill Gray, '01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College

body:
This is more than just bad leadership – it’s a total lack of transparency.

[](https://email.alert.freedomandlibertyreport.com/c/eJyUkbGu3CwQhZ8Gd6wwYOwtXPyS5eq_KdKktMYwXqOAsQZ8r_L2EdamSBmJ6mjmO4czPz6WD_DBH69vEHHcAi2U68t2j74UvgORz3yHT1ykkJqLJ5dmaRs3ivbptG5wbHvZq6ETrWj2UeDgsN9WPaiu34Z1QNPC0G1aa6uMhMaPlSOe0kihhHo-tG416g7MarZBbz3TAgJSeWyE6FKEwwW_IpVfhGei8rApNmHcSzkzU_8xOTM5Z7QX4ePLH4SuTlTt_YctEc94QEEm5z0Fx39ChAAcrE1XgTUghxMqSM1XiUuxTE3z_98l_xOVSUPVgfzxYmoqdCGTps5GdP6KTE0nRvDhreZ0kUWmJsrLjb5VC_EE_zqYmt7gbvkrzwnpOu5Ay3sNYjlT9sWne6uh0Z1fPgSfTS3qVT3vQsq_HO9zlL8DAAD__8i5pho)

It's no secret that Kamala Harris has been dodging the spotlight, but now it's reached a new level.

The Harris-Walz ticket is on pace to do fewer interviews and press conferences than any major party's presidential pairing in modern U.S. history. That raises a serious question: _**[What is Kamala hiding?](https://email.alert.freedomandlibertyreport.com/c/eJyUkbGu3CwQhZ8Gd6wwYOwtXPyS5eq_KdKktMYwXqOAsQZ8r_L2EdamSBmJ6mjmO4czPz6WD_DBH69vEHHcAi2U68t2j74UvgORz3yHT1ykkJqLJ5dmaRs3ivbptG5wbHvZq6ETrWj2UeDgsN9WPaiu34Z1QNPC0G1aa6uMhMaPlSOe0kihhHo-tG416g7MarZBbz3TAgJSeWyE6FKEwwW_IpVfhGei8rApNmHcSzkzU_8xOTM5Z7QX4ePLH4SuTlTt_YctEc94QEEm5z0Fx39ChAAcrE1XgTUghxMqSM1XiUuxTE3z_98l_xOVSUPVgfzxYmoqdCGTps5GdP6KTE0nRvDhreZ0kUWmJsrLjb5VC_EE_zqYmt7gbvkrzwnpOu5Ay3sNYjlT9sWne6uh0Z1fPgSfTS3qVT3vQsq_HO9zlL8DAAD__8i5pho)**_

[](https://email.alert.freedomandlibertyreport.com/c/eJyUkbGu3CwQhZ8Gd6wwYOwtXPyS5eq_KdKktMYwXqOAsQZ8r_L2EdamSBmJ6mjmO4czPz6WD_DBH69vEHHcAi2U68t2j74UvgORz3yHT1ykkJqLJ5dmaRs3ivbptG5wbHvZq6ETrWj2UeDgsN9WPaiu34Z1QNPC0G1aa6uMhMaPlSOe0kihhHo-tG416g7MarZBbz3TAgJSeWyE6FKEwwW_IpVfhGei8rApNmHcSzkzU_8xOTM5Z7QX4ePLH4SuTlTt_YctEc94QEEm5z0Fx39ChAAcrE1XgTUghxMqSM1XiUuxTE3z_98l_xOVSUPVgfzxYmoqdCGTps5GdP6KTE0nRvDhreZ0kUWmJsrLjb5VC_EE_zqYmt7gbvkrzwnpOu5Ay3sNYjlT9sWne6uh0Z1fPgSfTS3qVT3vQsq_HO9zlL8DAAD__8i5pho)
At a time when America is facing crisis after crisis - from skyrocketing inflation to an out-of-control border - Harris has chosen to hide from the public.

While President Trump is out front every day, fighting for the American people, Harris and her running mate are refusing to answer the tough questions.

This is more than just bad leadership - it's a total lack of transparency.

I've always believed that politicians owe the American people answers. Harris and Walz are doing the exact opposite. Their silence speaks volumes. _**[What are they afraid of? Peter, The choices we make in the closing weeks of this election will determine the kind of future we build for ourselves and our children. Today, I’m asking for your help with a project that’s near and dear to my heart: **putting an end to extreme partisan gerrymandering. ** It seems that Republicans have decided they can’t win on their ideas alone, so they’re trying to manipulate the maps and the rules in order to hold onto power. Every time they succeed, our democracy gets weaker. It’s not just about who gets representation and who doesn’t — it’s about the basic principle that holds the American experiment together: the idea that, in a democracy, _every voice matters._ Unfortunately, this issue just isn’t on the radar for most voters. That’s why it’s so important for the people who get it — and I’m looking at you, Peter — to do everything we can to stop politicians from picking their voters instead of the other way around. It means you have skin in the game. | Peter, The choices we make in the closing weeks of this election will determine the kind of future we build for ourselves and our children. Today, I’m asking for your help with a project that’s near and dear to my heart: putting an end to extreme partisan gerrymandering. It seems that Republicans have decided they can’t win on their ideas alone, so they’re trying to manipulate the maps and the rules in order to hold onto power. Every time they succeed, our democracy gets weaker. It’s not just about who gets representation and who doesn’t — it’s about the basic principle that holds the American experiment together: the idea that, in a democracy, every voice matters. Unfortunately, this issue just isn’t on the radar for most voters. That’s why it’s so important for the people who get it — and I’m looking at you, Peter — to do everything we can to stop politicians from picking their voters instead of the other way around. = | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = I want to be clear about one thing: A donation is about more than just the money. ### A story about the people who believed in and supported me when I was just a kid on Dunklin Street.

In ninth grade, I needed a hard lesson.
I was ashamed of where I came from.
My parents were recovering from a bankruptcy brought on by my littlest sister's heart surgery, her ongoing disability, and associated medical bills. We were broke, and it showed. I did what I could with my Salvation Army clothes and tried to hide as much of the rest as I could. Like our car, an old brown rusted out Ford van, that frequently rumbled and sputtered -- and had a knack for sliding out of service when we needed it the most and could least afford to fix it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/01021bb7-5cca-4075-bc95-e1facb3efb90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Kunce family van in front of the old house_
Through a combination of skill, charitable billing, and forgiven debts, our neighborhood mechanic, W, a minor hero of this story, kept us on the road. Given the nature of that relationship and our predicament, however, non-critical issues with the vehicle had to be tolerated, including a set of brakes that screeched horribly every time we slowed down. I kept this evidence of our financial predicament out of the public eye by having my dad, on days when he drove me to school, drop me off at the bottom of the hill, far from the front doors, and then dashing away from him and the van as quickly as possible.
The strategy worked. I made some friends, almost dated my first ninth grade crush, and raised my profile from bottom rung uncool to slightly below average.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4149d99b-fc12-4ece-949a-1d055895e7ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Lucas, 9th grade_
Then, a couple months into the year, I got my big break: I was assigned a project with J. J was a significantly cooler and surprisingly nice girl who lived across town by the mall and had attended our other middle school. Fortunately, this meant that she had no legacy impression of my social standing. One day, near the end of the project, she invited me over to her house to finish it.
_**It was a dream. **_
Her mom picked us up and drove us to their beautiful home in the fancy area of town. We breezed through the project, crushing name-brand snacks and soda (their house didn't have a single yellow box item in it!), sneaking in some TV time, and enjoying the afternoon. My imagination is filled with future visits, introductions to friends, and maybe the occasional party invitation.
After a few hours, her father, Mr. H, came through the garage door. Mr. H was, to capture it in one word, formidable. Tall, thick, deep-voiced, sincere, and, to me, imposing. He greeted me in a perfectly pleasant manner, and I replied as best I could, stuck somewhere between fear and awe.
He talked to Mrs. H for a bit while J and I wrapped things up, and then he came in and said something along the lines of "Son, you're welcome to stay, but I understand from Mrs. H that you're headed home for dinner?"
"Yes, Sir."
"Well, then let's get you on home."
That was the last thing I wanted. There was no way on earth that I was going to let J see my neighborhood or house yet, and I had prepared myself for this possibility.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/66984479-600c-43bf-985d-66b4d47e4036?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_The old house today_
"Oh no, don't worry, Sir, I told my dad I would call him when we were done. I'll walk down and he can pick me up on the corner."
Boom. Down on the corner. No view of our van. No view of our house or neighborhood. Foolproof.
_**Except ...**_
Mr. H was old school.
"No, no, no. There's no need to call your dad or for him to go to that trouble. You came over here to do the work. I'll give you a ride home."
I pushed back. "Really, Sir, it's ok. It won't be any trouble for him. If I could just use the phone..."
Mr. H looked at me like I had lost my mind.
"Son, you're our guest," he said with an indisputable tone of finality. "Let's load up."
J smiled at me. I smiled weakly back and followed her to the garage.
I wasn't sure if I should be thrilled or even more concerned, but inside was a big beautiful black Cadillac. J got into the front seat next to her dad and I opened the door behind her and climbed in. It was far and away the nicest car I had ever been in.
"Alright, where to?" he asked as he backed out of the driveway.
"We're on the east side past school," I replied, the wheels turning swiftly in my mind. "I can just give you directions if that'll work."
"That'll work."
It was nearly six o'clock and the sun was starting to go down. As we left their neighborhood I began plotting a course. I needed to eat up as much daylight as possible and avoid the worst landmarks on the way in. I knew I had to approach our house from the far side to avoid the corner gas station known locally as "ghetto" gas, but the street before ours was way too ragged, so I couldn't have him turn there. Plus that street had public housing on the other end that he might be aware of. The only real option was to loop all the way around the south side of town and then back up to my house from the east.
I gave him the occasional direction. Left. Right. Straight. A few blocks down. At first he followed the directions without paying attention, chatting with J and me about school and our day. But at some point he gave me a long look in the rearview mirror.
"Son, are you sure you know where you're headed?" He asked me after a particularly strange turn.
"Oh yes," I replied, "I've lived in the same neighborhood since we moved here when I was really little."
"Where is it again?"
"Kind of down from the highway patrol..." I answered, which was vague enough to encompass a massive area.
"Streets?"
"Dunklin... and... um... Ewing." Ewing was a super tiny street by that house basically no one would know.
He looked back at me again, but didn't say anything this time. >From that point on he let me guide him without question.
As we turned to go up the hill on Dunklin I felt a sense of relief. We had gone the nicest possible way and J had hardly paid attention. I winced a little as we rolled past the crumbling house two doors down from ours, but I diverted their attention by starting my good-byes and pointing ahead to our house so he would know where to stop. Following the line of my own finger, though, my heart sank. I never came up to our house from this side or paid attention to it, but that whole side was shedding paint. Like a molting lizard. Big chunks missing everywhere and paint scales just barely clinging to it.
My parents had recently done their best to paint the house -- my mom nearly caught it on fire at one point with a heat gun -- but they hadn't had the time or money to paint the entire thing.
So they hadn't done the east side, presumably reasoning that people rarely came that way and it was the least exposed.
As the car slowed to stop in front of our house, for the first time I really noticed everything that was wrong with it. The patchy yard. The broken curb and twisted sidewalk. I mumbled something nondescript about working on things or how busy everyone was or something like that, said a weak good-bye, and fled the car. I don't remember hearing anything from J or her father. I was just trying to get out of there and move them along as quickly as possible.
Then, as I walked down the front walk, I heard the worst noise imaginable: a second car door shutting behind me. As Johnny Cash would say, it echoed through the canyons like the disappearing dreams of yesterday. Someone else had gotten out. The sound took me to a new low.
With nowhere to go and nothing else to do, I fortified my will and, slowly, I turned around. Looming across the top of that big beautiful black Cadillac stood Mr. H, looking down at me. The car was still running. He had closed his door so that J wouldn't hear what he had to say.
"Son," he began, in his big deep voice. I forced myself to look at him. I was going to take it like a man, so he wouldn't think less of me.
He continued.
"I want you to know that we were honored to have you at the house today. I am glad I got to meet you and that you're my daughter's friend."
He paused, looking past me at our house, and then looked back down at me. With complete sincerity, that I believed in my soul, he added: "You have a beautiful home and you're going to do great things. I'm proud to know you and I'd be proud for J to come back anytime."
He didn't wait for me to respond. That was it. He just opened the door back up, climbed in, and put the car in gear. J waved as they drove away, obviously not noticing a thing.
To this day I tear up when I think about that moment. The moment when a man I didn't know made the effort to understand me. And then took a moment to let me know, without telling me directly, that I could be proud of who I was and where I came from.
That lesson couldn't have come from my family. It couldn't have come from inside the world I lived in. It had to come from outside. And if it hadn't been for Mr. H, I don't know if I would have ever been comfortable enough to just be me.
I never saw him again, but that year was a turning point for me, a kid who had been entirely undistinguished up to that point.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/aac86d7c-33d7-4975-b6b8-7b1ee0b513ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_At a turning point_
I studied hard and practiced hard. I made it to Yale on a Pell Grant. I went to that fancy east coast school and was never shy about where I came from and who I was. And then I came back home to mid-Missouri for law school. It's where my roots were. My grandparents were in the early stages of Alzheimer's there and there was nowhere else I wanted to be.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/209695de-e0b6-4f98-84e1-31e60d91b37f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Lucas and Grandparents_
This was my world.
I looked up Mr. H. I wanted to tell him thank you. For everything. For lifting up a kid he didn't know when he didn't have to. But I never got a chance. He passed away unexpectedly while I was at school.
Now, I make sure his legacy lives through me by never missing an opportunity to lift a kid up and let him know that he can be proud of where he comes from. This is the legacy I will bring to the United States Senate.

I knew I had to approach our house from the far side to avoid the corner gas station known locally as "ghetto" gas, but the street before ours was way too ragged, so I couldn't have him turn there. Plus that street had public housing on the other end that he might be aware of. The only real option was to loop all the way around the south side of town and then back up to my house from the east. I gave him the occasional direction. Left. Right. Straight. A few blocks down. At first he followed the directions without paying attention, chatting with J and me about school and our day. But at some point he gave me a long look in the rearview mirror. "Son, are you sure you know where you're headed?" He asked me after a particularly strange turn. "Oh yes," I replied, "I've lived in the same neighborhood since we moved here when I was really little." "Where is it again?" "Kind of down from the highway patrol..." I answered, which was vague enough to encompass a massive area. "Streets?" "Dunklin... and... um... Ewing." Ewing was a super tiny street by that house basically no one would know. He looked back at me again, but didn't say anything this time. >From that point on he let me guide him without question. As we turned to go up the hill on Dunklin I felt a sense of relief. We had gone the nicest possible way and J had hardly paid attention. I winced a little as we rolled past the crumbling house two doors down from ours, but I diverted their attention by starting my good-byes and pointing ahead to our house so he would know where to stop. Following the line of my own finger, though, my heart sank. I never came up to our house from this side or paid attention to it, but that whole side was shedding paint. Like a molting lizard. Big chunks missing everywhere and paint scales just barely clinging to it. My parents had recently done their best to paint the house -- my mom nearly caught it on fire at one point with a heat gun -- but they hadn't had the time or money to paint the entire thing. So they hadn't done the east side, presumably reasoning that people rarely came that way and it was the least exposed. As the car slowed to stop in front of our house, for the first time I really noticed everything that was wrong with it. The patchy yard. The broken curb and twisted sidewalk. I mumbled something nondescript about working on things or how busy everyone was or something like that, said a weak good-bye, and fled the car. I don't remember hearing anything from J or her father. I was just trying to get out of there and move them along as quickly as possible. Then, as I walked down the front walk, I heard the worst noise imaginable: a second car door shutting behind me. As Johnny Cash would say, it echoed through the canyons like the disappearing dreams of yesterday. Someone else had gotten out. The sound took me to a new low. With nowhere to go and nothing else to do, I fortified my will and, slowly, I turned around. Looming across the top of that big beautiful black Cadillac stood Mr. H, looking down at me. The car was still running. He had closed his door so that J wouldn't hear what he had to say. "Son," he began, in his big deep voice. I forced myself to look at him. I was going to take it like a man, so he wouldn't think less of me. He continued. "I want you to know that we were honored to have you at the house today. I am glad I got to meet you and that you're my daughter's friend." He paused, looking past me at our house, and then looked back down at me. With complete sincerity, that I believed in my soul, he added: "You have a beautiful home and you're going to do great things. I'm proud to know you and I'd be proud for J to come back anytime." He didn't wait for me to respond. That was it. He just opened the door back up, climbed in, and put the car in gear. J waved as they drove away, obviously not noticing a thing. To this day I tear up when I think about that moment. The moment when a man I didn't know made the effort to understand me. And then took a moment to let me know, without telling me directly, that I could be proud of who I was and where I came from. That lesson couldn't have come from my family. It couldn't have come from inside the world I lived in. It had to come from outside. And if it hadn't been for Mr. H, I don't know if I would have ever been comfortable enough to just be me. I never saw him again, but that year was a turning point for me, a kid who had been entirely undistinguished up to that point. | | ---|---|--- At a turning point I studied hard and practiced hard. I made it to Yale on a Pell Grant. I went to that fancy east coast school and was never shy about where I came from and who I was. And then I came back home to mid-Missouri for law school. It's where my roots were. My grandparents were in the early stages of Alzheimer's there and there was nowhere else I wanted to be. | | ---|---|--- Lucas and Grandparents This was my world. I looked up Mr. H. I wanted to tell him thank you. For everything. For lifting up a kid he didn't know when he didn't have to. But I never got a chance. He passed away unexpectedly while I was at school. Now, I make sure his legacy lives through me by never missing an opportunity to lift a kid up and let him know that he can be proud of where he comes from. This is the legacy I will bring to the United States Senate. body:
Today we’re launching our second broadcast ad for the general election!
#
We have some exciting news!
**Today we’re launching our second broadcast ad for the general election!** This new ad highlights the support Sarah has received from working people and union members across Delaware. Take a look:
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mcb-em-20240926-1?refcode=em20240926-1-1277&amount=5&refcode2=1277_21716_bcqBFM&akid=1277%2E21716%2EbcqBFM)
**[Donate $5 »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mcb-em-20240926-1?amount=5&refcode=em20240926-1-1277&refcode2=1277_21716_bcqBFM&akid=1277%2E21716%2EbcqBFM)**
Whether it’s helping to raise the **minimum wage** , passing **paid family and medical leave** , or **working across the aisle** with Republicans, workers know that Sarah is going to DC to deliver for working families like theirs.
It makes for a stark contrast with Sarah’s Republican opponent, who just endorsed the Project 2025 plan to undo progress on the right to organize, empower union busters, and gut the NLRB’s enforcement capacity.
It’s clear that Sarah is the best choice to represent Delaware’s working people in Congress. So here at McBride HQ, it’s all hands on deck until Election Day, and we’re counting on your support to keep this campaign going strong!
[**If you’re ready to send Sarah to Congress to get big things done for working people in Delaware and across the country, will you pitch in $5 today?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mcb-em-20240926-1?refcode=em20240926-1-1277&amount=5&refcode2=1277_21716_bcqBFM&akid=1277%2E21716%2EbcqBFM)

Thank you, and stay tuned for more updates soon!
Team McBride

TO: Congressman Eric Sorensen
FROM: Carter Elliott, Campaign Manager
DATE: Thursday, September 26, 2024
6 WEEKS FROM ELECTION DAY
_Strategic Overview of the Final Weeks of the Race_
Congressman Sorensen,
Please find below the **Internal Campaign Update.**
**Updates:**
* National Republicans have made a joint TV buy with our opponent, Joe McGraw – their first of the cycle – dropping over a quarter million dollars across all three of our media markets.
* National Republicans are struggling to fundraise and have limited resources, so their major investment in IL-17 shows this race is at the top of their priority list.

**Takeaways:**
* With National Democrats remaining focused on challenging incumbent Republicans, our campaign is on our own to push back against this incoming Republican spending.
* In 2022, National Republicans spent $12 million dollars and, with the help of National Democrats, we were able to match that spending and win. This year, though, Republicans look to be prepared to spend at 2022 levels, while National Democrats are not.

**Strategy:**
* The bottom line is: **if we are going to be without the support of National Democrats, we are going to need to make up the difference on our own.**
* To keep up with Republican spending, we’ve strengthened all of our paid communications plans, especially on broadcast TV, but we now have a $200k budget gap we have to make up.

This race is shifting fast and we have to move quickly to stay ahead of Republicans and get our positive message out. We need to make sure every one of our supporters know what we’re up against.
If you have any questions, please feel free to respond here.
Thanks,
Carter

**The small rural town of Bloomsburg shaped who I am. I 'm proud to be a 7th-generation Pennsylvania and I'm ready to get to work to help the great people of our state.**

_**BUT, I am worried that the American Dream is slipping away.**_**Career politicians like my opponent Bob Casey and Kamala Harris are doing NOTHING to stop inflation, allowing rampant crime to go unchecked, and allowing dangerous drugs to cross our borders in excess.** Their policies have made America weaker, and I can't sit back and let that happen. clean_body: I recently went to my home county fair, and it got me thinking about the small town of Bloomsburg, Pennsylvania Peter, I recently went to my home county fair, and it got me thinking about how the small town of Bloomsburg, Pennsylvania and the great people of my county helped shape who I am today. I know this is a long message, but I hope you will read it all the way to the end. Growing up, my family lived on campus at Bloomsburg State College and my parents owned a farm ten minutes down the road. I had summer jobs baling hay and trimming Christmas trees at nearby farms. My dad started his career teaching history, economics, & democracy at Punxsutawney High. My mom began teaching fourth through sixth graders at a public school near Pittsburgh. I'm incredibly proud that my dad was chosen to be president of Bloomsburg State College (now Bloomsburg University) at only 34 years old. I'm so proud of my parents' teaching careers and to have been raised in Bloomsburg. It was there that I wrestled and played football and was nominated to the U.S. Military Academy at West Point. And it was there that I came home to a parade after serving in combat during the Gulf War. The small rural town of Bloomsburg shaped who I am. I 'm proud to be a 7th-generation Pennsylvania and I'm ready to get to work to help the great people of our state. All this is to say, I've lived the American Dream, and I am so grateful for the opportunities that America and Pennsylvania have afforded me. BUT, I am worried that the American Dream is slipping away.Career politicians like my opponent Bob Casey and Kamala Harris are doing NOTHING to stop inflation, allowing rampant crime to go unchecked, and allowing dangerous drugs to cross our borders in excess. Their policies have made America weaker, and I can't sit back and let that happen. I'm running for U.S. Senate to shake up the status quo. Friends,
It’s official: Jim Jordan is scared. I told you! HA!
We just found out that, for the first time in his political career, he’s polling the district to determine how much trouble he’s in.
And get this! His pollsters are even asking voters if they have any dirt on me.
I live a pretty boring life, so good luck with that. If they have me followed their calls would go like this, “No, she’s single and seems to have no personal life. Sorry sir, when she’s home she’s busy on the phone or computer strategizing how to take you down, or when she’s out she’s talking to voters, winning them over, that’s literally all she does.” 😂
The truth is they’re digging for dirt they’ll never find because they know our message is resonating, and they’re desperate.
OMG I love this so much!! He’s going down and he knows it!!! Everyone here feels it! I wish you were here so you could feel it too!
Our own latest polling shows we’re statistically tied with Jordan – no wonder he’s scrambling!
He knows the people of this district are waking up to his complete fraud and failure of his job performance in Congress and his dangerous agenda of gutting Social Security and Medicare , attacking women’s righ ts , and blocking critical funding for our farmers and veterans.

Jordan’s pollsters are trying to find something to use to smear me because they know they can’t win on the issues.
Frankly, they’re scared, and they should be.

This is the most important congressional race in the country, and together, we can finally take Jim Jordan down.

Dear Peter,
Where evergreen meets ocean blue, you’ll find a California original: the redwood forests of the Sonoma Coast. This rugged wilderness is one of the treasured few of its kind — an area rich in history, biodiversity, and unmatched beauty.
Sonoma Coast Redwoods is home to some of the oldest second-growth redwoods in the range, standing guard for hundreds of years, side-by-side with new-growth trees, young saplings and old-growth mother trees. [**This is a forest set to _thrive_ in the decades to come — _if we can protect it_.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/93656741/501188905/-2057046435?contactdata=iJOTve9Op2tEKSATObSMcVa8PVWivvtQqx7y9FqciwafQyVuYl2hFYT5QsjFP102oGq25McerxFZ4gd6V0zJJh1xaZiwfM7FnjWAy7WGG010WIO6KVQG5EutiMQgE2axy9wO1WlpnVYoBjZpSRtHF6OZtZ/z3UJDIik+19f1kC4=&ms=SCR2_Link1&sourceid=1165968&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9TVFJXTC9TVFJXTC8xLzg5NTc0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImIyN2FiNzUzLTRlN2MtZWYxMS04NDczLTYwNDViZGE4YWEzNCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=dZaKfMB69P9dy8BSioA-d-ihxkckKVqqcYjlvRFYL0k=&emci=1b440787-767b-ef11-991a-6045bdee6681&emdi=b27ab753-4e7c-ef11-8473-6045bda8aa34&ceid=1504551)

Sonoma Coast Redwoods is of the _highest conservation priority_ because of its incredible carbon-storage potential. Reconnecting these lands to the larger redwood corridor would secure the region’s redwood footprint — and protect the Sonoma Coast Redwoods property from harmful development.
**There are those who would love to build homes and private estates here.
